units.zh: 宣秉字巨公，馮翊雲陽人也。
units.en: Xuan Bing, styled Jugong, came from Yunyang in Fengyi.
units.literal: Xuan Bing, courtesy name Jugong, was a man of Yunyang in Fengyi commandery.

units.zh: 少修高節，顯名三輔。
units.en: From his youth he upheld a stern moral standard and made a name for himself across the Three Adjuncts.
units.literal: In youth he cultivated lofty integrity and became famous in the Three Adjuncts.

units.zh: 哀、平際，見王氏據權專政，侵削宗室，有逆亂萌，遂隱遁深山，州郡連召，常稱疾不仕。
units.en: Under Emperors Ai and Ping, when he saw the Wang family monopolize power, chip away at the imperial clan, and the makings of revolt take shape, he withdrew to the deep hills; though province after province called him to serve, he always pleaded illness and stayed out of office.
units.literal: Between the reigns of Ai and Ping, seeing the Wang clan seize power and monopolize government, encroach on and diminish the imperial house, and the sprouts of rebellion and disorder appear, he thereupon hid himself in deep mountains; the province and commanderies summoned him in succession, but he constantly claimed illness and did not take office.

units.zh: 王莽為宰衡，辟命不應。
units.en: When Wang Mang held the title of supreme minister and summoned him to office, he refused the appointment.
units.literal: When Wang Mang was Grand Regent, he summoned him with a commission, but he did not respond.

units.zh: 及莽篡位，又遣使者征之，秉固稱疾病。
units.en: After Wang Mang seized the throne and again sent envoys for him, Xuan Bing insisted he was too ill to come.
units.literal: When Mang usurped the throne, he again sent envoys to summon him, but Bing firmly claimed illness.

units.zh: 更始即位，征為侍中。
units.en: When the Gengshi Emperor took the throne, Xuan Bing was called to court as a palace attendant.
units.literal: When Gengshi ascended the throne, he was summoned to be Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 建武元年，拜禦史中丞。
units.en: In Jianwu 1 he was named imperial clerk grandee.
units.literal: In the first year of Jianwu, he was appointed Imperial Clerk Grandee.

units.zh: 光武特詔禦史中丞與司隸校尉、尚書令會同並專席而坐，故京師號曰『三獨坐』。
units.en: Emperor Guangwu issued a special order that the imperial clerk grandee, the metropolitan commandant, and the director of the secretariat should hold joint sessions, each with his own seat—hence the capital nickname 'the three solitary seats.'
units.literal: Guangwu specially issued an edict that the Imperial Clerk Grandee, the Metropolitan Commandant, and the Director of the Secretariat should meet and sit each on a separate mat; therefore in the capital they were called the 'Three Solitary Seats.'

units.zh: 明年，遷司隸校尉。
units.en: The following year he was promoted to metropolitan commandant.
units.literal: The next year, he was transferred to Metropolitan Commandant.

units.zh: 務舉大綱，簡略苛細，百僚敬之。
units.en: He focused on the broad principles of government and eased petty severity, and the whole bureaucracy stood in awe of him.
units.literal: He strove to lift up the great principles and was lenient toward harsh minutiae; the hundred officials revered him.

units.zh: 秉性節約，常服布被，蔬食瓦器。
units.en: By temperament he was austere: he slept under a cotton quilt, ate simple fare, and used plain pottery at table.
units.literal: Bing by nature was frugal; he constantly used a cloth quilt, ate plain food, and used earthenware vessels.

units.zh: 帝嘗幸其府舍，見而嘆曰：『楚國二龔，不如雲陽宣巨公。』
units.en: The emperor once called at his home, looked about, and exclaimed, 'The two Gongs of Chu cannot match Jugong Xuan of Yunyang.'
units.literal: The emperor once visited his residence and, seeing it, sighed, saying, 'The two Gongs of Chu are not equal to Jugong Xuan of Yunyang.'

units.zh: 即賜布帛帳帷什物。
units.en: He then gave him cloth and silk, bed hangings, and other household goods.
units.literal: Thereupon he bestowed cloth, silk, curtains, hangings, and assorted goods.

units.zh: 四年，拜大司徒司直。
units.en: In the fourth year he was appointed Director to the Grand Minister over the Masses.
units.literal: In the fourth year, he was appointed Si Zhi of the Grand Minister over the Masses.

units.zh: 所得祿奉，輒以收養親族。
units.en: He turned every stipend he earned toward supporting his extended family.
units.literal: Whatever salary he received, he always used it to support and raise his kinsmen.

units.zh: 其孤弱者，分與田地，自無擔石之儲。
units.en: The orphaned and helpless he supplied with land, while he himself kept not even a peck of grain in reserve.
units.literal: To the orphaned and weak he allotted fields and land; he himself had no store even of a dan or shi of grain.

units.zh: 六年，卒於官，帝敏惜之，除子彪為郎。
units.en: He died in office in the sixth year; the emperor mourned him deeply and appointed his son Xuan Biao a gentleman cadet.
units.literal: In the sixth year, he died in office; the emperor grieved for him with keen regret and appointed his son Biao Gentleman.

units.zh: 張湛字子孝，扶風平陵人也。
units.en: Zhang Zhan, styled Zixiao, was a native of Pingling in Fufeng.
units.literal: Zhang Zhan, courtesy name Zixiao, was a man of Pingling in Fufeng commandery.

units.zh: 矜嚴好禮，動止有則，居處幽室，必自修整，雖遇妻子，若嚴君焉。
units.en: Grave in manner and devoted to ceremony, he regulated every gesture; even in his private rooms he kept himself in perfect order, and before his wife and children he behaved like a magistrate before his subordinates.
units.literal: He was stern and fond of ritual; in movement and rest he had rules; in dwelling in a secluded chamber he always put himself in order; even when facing wife and children, he was like a stern lord.

units.zh: 及在鄉黨，詳言正色，三輔以為儀表。
units.en: Among neighbors and townsfolk he chose his words carefully and kept a straight face, and the Three Adjuncts looked to him as their standard.
units.literal: When among the village and community, he spoke in detail with a straight countenance; the Three Adjuncts took him as a model.

units.zh: 人或謂湛偽詐，湛聞而笑曰：『我誠詐也。
units.en: Some called his manner a pose; when Zhang Zhan heard this he laughed and said, 'They are right—I am putting on an act.'
units.literal: Some people said Zhan was false and deceitful; Zhan heard it and laughed, saying, 'I am indeed deceitful.'

units.zh: 人皆詐惡，我獨詐善，不亦可乎？』
units.en: Everyone else pretends to be wicked; I alone pretend to be good—what is wrong with that?'
units.literal: All others feign wickedness; I alone feign goodness—is that not acceptable?'

units.zh: 成、哀間，為二千石。
units.en: Under Emperors Cheng and Ai he served in posts of two thousand piculs.
units.literal: Between Cheng and Ai, he held office at two thousand piculs rank.

units.zh: 王莽時，歷太守、都尉。
units.en: During Wang Mang's reign he successively held the posts of grand administrator and chief commandant.
units.literal: In the time of Wang Mang, he successively served as grand administrator and chief commandant.

units.zh: 建武初，為左馮翊，在郡修典禮，設條教，政化大行。
units.en: Early in Jianwu he became left administrator of Fengyi, where he revived the classical rituals, issued clear regulations, and saw a thorough moral transformation of the region.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, he was left Administrator of Fengyi; in the commandery he restored canonical rites, set down regulations and instruction, and administrative transformation was greatly carried out.

units.zh: 後告歸平陵，望寺門而步。
units.en: Later he took leave and returned to Pingling; when he reached the yamen gate he dismounted and went in on foot.
units.literal: Later he requested leave and returned to Pingling; facing the gate of the official residence he walked on foot.

units.zh: 主簿進曰：『明府位尊德重，不宜自輕。』
units.en: His chief clerk urged him: 'Your honor's rank and virtue are too high for you to demean yourself so.'
units.literal: The chief clerk advanced and said, 'My lord's position is exalted and your virtue weighty; it is not fitting to slight yourself.'

units.zh: 湛曰：『《禮》，下公門，軾輅馬。
units.en: Zhang Zhan replied, 'The Classic of Rites says that below a noble's gate one leaves the chariot and touches the crossbar in respect.'
units.literal: Zhan said, 'In the Classic of Rites, below the duke's gate one dismounts and leans on the carriage bar.'

units.zh: 孔子於鄉黨，恂恂如也。
units.en: Confucius among his neighbors was modest and careful in every step.
units.literal: Confucius in the village and community was deferential and cautious.

units.zh: 父母之國，所宜盡禮，何謂輕哉？』
units.en: In one's native place one should observe every courtesy—how is that belittling myself?'
units.literal: In the land of one's father and mother, one ought to exhaust ritual; what is called slighting?'

units.zh: 五年，拜光祿勛。
units.en: In the fifth year he was appointed Superintendent of the Imperial Household (Guanglu Xun).
units.literal: In the fifth year, he was appointed Bearer of the Brightness.

units.zh: 光武臨朝，或有惰容，湛輒陳諫其失。
units.en: Whenever Emperor Guangwu looked slack at audience, Zhang Zhan would speak up and correct him.
units.literal: When Guangwu held court, sometimes there was a slack expression; Zhan always remonstrated by stating his faults.

units.zh: 常乘白馬，帝每見湛，輒言『白馬生且復諫矣』。
units.en: He habitually rode a white horse, so whenever the emperor saw him coming he would mutter, 'Here comes the white horse—ready to lecture me again.'
units.literal: He constantly rode a white horse; whenever the emperor saw Zhan, he would say, 'The white-horse gentleman is about to remonstrate again.'

units.zh: 七年，以病乞身，拜光祿大夫，代王丹為太子太傅。
units.en: In the seventh year he asked to retire on grounds of ill health; the court named him grandee of the imperial household and tutor to the crown prince in place of Wang Dan.
units.literal: In the seventh year, citing illness he begged to retire; he was appointed Grandee of the Imperial Household and replaced Wang Dan as tutor to the heir apparent.

units.zh: 及郭后廢，因稱疾不朝，拜太中大夫，居中東門候舍，故時人號曰中東門君。
units.en: After Empress Guo was cast aside he stayed away from court, pleading sickness; he was made grandee of the palace and lived in the lodge at the Central East Gate, so contemporaries dubbed him 'the lord of Central East Gate.'
units.literal: When Empress Guo was deposed, he thereupon claimed illness and did not attend court; he was appointed Grandee of the Palace and dwelt in the hostel at the Central East Gate, so people of the time called him Lord Central East Gate.

units.zh: 帝數存問賞賜。
units.en: The emperor often sent messengers to ask after his health and showered him with gifts.
units.literal: The emperor repeatedly inquired after him with gifts.

units.zh: 後大徒戴涉被誅，帝強起湛以代之。
units.en: Later, when Grand Minister of Education Dai She was put to death, the emperor insisted on dragging Zhang Zhan from retirement to fill the post.
units.literal: Later Grand Minister of Education Dai She was executed; the emperor forced Zhan to rise and replace him.

units.zh: 湛至朝堂，遺失溲便，因自陳疾篤，不能復任朝事，遂罷之。
units.en: At the hall of state he suffered a public loss of bladder control; he then declared himself too ill for any further duty and was allowed to step down.
units.literal: When Zhan reached the court hall, he lost control of his bladder; thereupon he himself stated his illness was grave and he could not again take up court affairs, and he was thereupon dismissed.

units.zh: 後數年，卒於家。
units.en: A few years later he died at home.
units.literal: Several years later, he died at home.

units.zh: 王丹字仲回，京兆下邽人也。
units.en: Wang Dan, styled Zhonghui, came from Xiaqi in the Jingzhao area around the capital.
units.literal: Wang Dan, courtesy name Zhonghui, was a man of Xiaqi in the metropolitan region of Jingzhao.

units.zh: 哀、平時，仕州郡。
units.en: Under Emperors Ai and Ping he held office in provincial and commandery administration.
units.literal: In the time of Ai and Ping, he served in province and commandery.

units.zh: 王莽時，連征不至。
units.en: Wang Mang summoned him repeatedly, but he never answered the call.
units.literal: In the time of Wang Mang, he was repeatedly summoned but did not arrive.

units.zh: 家累千金，隱居養誌，好施周急。
units.en: Though his household was worth a thousand pounds of gold, he lived in retirement, nurturing his aims, generous to those in sudden need.
units.literal: His family accumulated wealth to a thousand in gold; he lived in reclusion cultivating his purpose, was fond of giving and relieving the urgent.

units.zh: 每歲農時，輒載酒肴於田間，候勤者而勞之。
units.en: Each spring he would drive wine and meat to the fields and toast the hardest-working farmers.
units.literal: Every year at farming season, he would load wine and food in the fields and wait for the diligent and reward them.

units.zh: 其墮懶者，恥不致丹，皆兼功自厲。
units.en: The idle felt ashamed to fall short of his example and doubled their efforts.
units.literal: Those who were lazy were ashamed not to reach Dan's standard, and all doubled their effort and urged themselves on.

units.zh: 邑聚相率，以致殷富。
units.en: Hamlet after hamlet took his lead and grew prosperous.
units.literal: Villages and hamlets led one another and thereby became abundant and rich.

units.zh: 其輕黠遊蕩廢業為患者，輒曉其父兄，使黜責之。
units.en: Young men who loafed, schemed, and made trouble he would take aside with their fathers and elder brothers until they were chastened back to work.
units.literal: As for those who were frivolous, cunning, roamed and wandered, abandoned their work and became a harm, he always enlightened their fathers and brothers and made them dismiss and reprove them.

units.zh: 沒者則賻給，親自將護。
units.en: For the dead he paid burial costs and saw to the rites himself.
units.literal: Those who died, he assisted with funeral gifts and personally oversaw the arrangements.

units.zh: 其有遭喪憂者，輒待丹為辦，鄉鄰以為常。
units.en: Families in mourning learned to wait for Wang Dan to arrange everything; neighbors came to expect it.
units.literal: Those who suffered bereavement and grief always waited for Dan to handle it; the village neighbors took it as normal.

units.zh: 行之十餘年，其化大洽，風俗以篤。
units.en: He kept this up for over a decade until custom ran deep and the whole countryside grew earnest and kind.
units.literal: He practiced this for more than ten years; his transformation was greatly harmonious and customs thereby became earnest.

units.zh: 丹資性方潔，疾惡強豪。
units.en: Wang Dan was square and scrupulous by nature, and detested bullies and grandees.
units.literal: Dan by nature was upright and clean, hated the evil and the powerful and grand.

units.zh: 時，河南太守同郡陳遵，關西之大俠也。
units.en: At the time Chen Zun, grand administrator of Henan and a fellow townsman, was famed as the greatest bravo west of the passes.
units.literal: At that time the grand administrator of Henan, Chen Zun of the same commandery, was a great knight-errant west of the pass.

units.zh: 其友人喪親，遵為護喪事，賻助甚豐。
units.en: When a friend's parent died, Chen Zun staged the funeral and poured in lavish contributions.
units.literal: When a friend of his lost a parent, Zun undertook the funeral affairs for him, and the condolence gifts were very abundant.

units.zh: 丹乃懷縑一匹，陳之於主人前，曰：『如丹此縑，出自機杼。』
units.en: Wang Dan brought only a single bolt of silk, laid it before the bereaved family, and said, 'This cloth is thread I wove myself.'
units.literal: Dan then carried in his bosom one bolt of silk, displayed it before the host, and said, 'Such silk as Dan has here comes from the loom.'

units.zh: 遵聞而有慚色。
units.en: Chen Zun flushed with shame when he heard that.
units.literal: When Zun heard, he had a look of shame.

units.zh: 自以知名，欲結交於丹，丹拒而不許。
units.en: Confident in his own reputation, Chen Zun sought Wang Dan's friendship; Wang Dan turned him down flat.
units.literal: Considering himself famous, he wished to befriend Dan, but Dan refused and did not permit it.

units.zh: 會前將軍鄧禹西征關中，軍糧乏，丹率宗族上表二千斛。
units.en: When General Deng Yu marched into Guanzhong and supplies ran short, Wang Dan led his kinsmen in offering two thousand hu of grain to the throne.
units.literal: When former general Deng Yu campaigned west into Guanzhong, army provisions were lacking; Dan led his clan to present a memorial offering two thousand hu of grain.

units.zh: 禹在領左馮翊，稱疾不視事，免歸。
units.en: Deng Yu was also left administrator of Fengyi; he pleaded illness, neglected the yamen, and was removed to go home.
units.literal: Yu was concurrently left Administrator of Fengyi; he claimed illness and did not attend to affairs, and was dismissed and returned home.

units.zh: 後征為太子少傅。
units.en: Later Wang Dan was recalled as junior tutor to the crown prince.
units.literal: Later he was summoned to be Junior Tutor to the heir apparent.

units.zh: 時，大司徒侯霸欲與交友，及丹被征，遣子昱候於道。
units.en: Grand Minister Hou Ba wanted his friendship; when Wang Dan was summoned to court, Hou sent his son Hou Yu to greet him on the road.
units.literal: At that time Grand Minister of Education Hou Ba wished to befriend him, and when Dan was summoned, he sent his son Yu to wait on the road.

units.zh: 昱迎拜車下，丹下答之。
units.en: Hou Yu bowed at the carriage step; Wang Dan stepped down and returned the courtesy.
units.literal: Yu greeted and bowed below the carriage; Dan descended and returned the bow.

units.zh: 昱曰：『家公欲與君結交，何為見拜？』
units.en: Hou Yu said, 'My father means to befriend you—why do you bow back as if to an equal?'
units.literal: Yu said, 'My father wishes to befriend you; why do you return the bow?'

units.zh: 丹曰：『君房有是言，丹未之許也。』
units.en: Wang Dan replied, 'If your father said that, I have never agreed to it.'
units.literal: Dan said, 'If Junfang had such words, Dan has not assented to them.'

units.zh: 丹子有同門生喪家，家在中山，白丹欲往奔慰。
units.en: Wang Dan's son had a classmate whose family was in mourning in Zhongshan; the boy asked leave to rush there in person.
units.literal: Dan's son had a fellow student whose family had a bereavement; the home was in Zhongshan, and he informed Dan wishing to go hasten to console.

units.zh: 結侶將行，丹怒而撻之，令寄縑以祠焉。
units.en: He was gathering travel companions when Wang Dan beat him in anger and told him to send a bolt of silk for the rites instead.
units.literal: He tied companions and was about to set out; Dan angrily flogged him and ordered him to send silk by post for sacrifice there.

units.zh: 或問其故，丹曰：『交道之難，未易言也。
units.en: Asked why, Wang Dan said, 'The pitfalls of friendship are not easily put into words.'
units.literal: Someone asked the reason; Dan said, 'The difficulty of friendship is not easy to speak of.'

units.zh: 世稱管、鮑，次則王、貢。
units.en: The world praises Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya; next come Wang Ji and Gong Yu.
units.literal: The age praises Guan and Bao; next come Wang and Gong.

units.zh: 張、陳兇其終，蕭，朱隙其末，故知全之者鮮矣。』
units.en: Zhang Er and Chen Yu destroyed each other; Xiao Yu and Zhu Bo fell out at the end—so few friendships stay whole."
units.literal: Zhang and Chen came to a disastrous end in their friendship; Xiao and Zhu fell out at the last—therefore one knows those who preserve friendship to the end are few."

units.zh: 時人服其言。
units.en: His contemporaries conceded the point.
units.literal: People of the time submitted to his words.

units.zh: 客初有薦士於丹者，因選舉之，而後所舉者陷罪，丹坐以免。
units.en: A retainer once recommended a man whom Wang Dan then advanced; when that man was later convicted, Wang Dan lost his post on account of it.
units.literal: A client at first had recommended a scholar to Dan; thereupon he selected and raised him, but afterward the one he had raised was implicated in a crime, and Dan sat for it and was dismissed.

units.zh: 客慚懼自絕，而丹終無所言。
units.en: The retainer, mortified, cut off all contact, yet Wang Dan never breathed a word of reproach.
units.literal: The client was ashamed and afraid and broke off relations of himself, but Dan to the end said nothing.

units.zh: 尋復征為太子太傅，乃呼客謂曰：『子之自絕，何量丹之薄也？』
units.en: Soon recalled as tutor to the crown prince, he summoned the same retainer and said, 'You dropped me as if I were too small-minded to understand?'
units.literal: Soon he was again summoned as tutor to the heir apparent; he then called the client and said, 'Your breaking off—how could you think Dan so petty?'

units.zh: 不為設食以罰之，相待如舊。
units.en: He withheld a meal as a light rebuke, then treated him exactly as before.
units.literal: He did not set out food for him as a punishment, but treated him as before.

units.zh: 其後遜位，卒於家。
units.en: He later resigned his post and died at home.
units.literal: Afterward he yielded his position and died at home.

units.zh: 王良字仲子，東海蘭陵人也。
units.en: Wang Liang, styled Zhongzi, was from Lanling in Donghai.
units.literal: Wang Liang, courtesy name Zhongzi, was a man of Lanling in Donghai commandery.

units.zh: 少好學，習《小夏侯尚書》。
units.en: In youth he loved learning and mastered the Lesser Xiahou version of the Documents.
units.literal: In youth he was fond of learning and studied the Lesser Xiahou Documents.

units.zh: 王莽時，寢病不仕，教授諸生千餘人。
units.en: Under Wang Mang he stayed in bed and refused office, while instructing over a thousand pupils.
units.literal: In the time of Wang Mang, he lay ill and did not take office, and taught more than a thousand students.

units.zh: 建武二年，大司馬吳漢辟，不應。
units.en: In Jianwu 2 Grand Marshal Wu Han offered him a post; he declined.
units.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, Grand Marshal Wu Han summoned him; he did not respond.

units.zh: 三年，征拜諫議太夫，數有忠言，以禮進止，朝廷敬之。
units.en: In the third year he was called to be grandee remonstrant; he spoke frankly, observed every ritual nicety in court, and the bureaucracy respected him.
units.literal: In the third year, he was summoned and appointed Grandee Remonstrant; he repeatedly had loyal words, advanced and withdrew according to ritual, and the court revered him.

units.zh: 遷沛郡太守。
units.en: He was then moved to grand administrator of Pei.
units.literal: He was transferred to grand administrator of Pei commandery.

units.zh: 至蘄縣，稱病不之府，官屬皆隨就之，良遂上疾篤，乞骸骨，征拜太中大夫。
units.en: At Qi he pleaded illness and never entered the yamen; his staff trooped out to him instead. He then memorialized that he was dying, asked to retire, and was made grandee of the palace.
units.literal: When he reached Qi county, he claimed illness and did not go to the official residence; the subordinate officials all followed and went to him; Liang thereupon submitted that his illness was grave, begged for his bones, and was summoned and appointed Grandee of the Palace.

units.zh: 六年，代宣秉為大司徒司直。
units.en: In the sixth year he succeeded Xuan Bing as grandee of the grand minister of education for directorships.
units.literal: In the sixth year, he replaced Xuan Bing as Grandee of the Grand Minister of Education for Directorships.

units.zh: 在位恭儉，妻子不入官舍，布被瓦器。
units.en: In office he was humble and spare: his wife and children never set foot in the yamen, and his quarters held only a cotton quilt and pottery vessels.
units.literal: In position he was respectful and frugal; wife and children did not enter the official residence; he had a cloth quilt and earthenware vessels.

units.zh: 時，司徒史鮑恢以事到東海，過候其家，而良妻布裙曳柴，從田中歸。
units.en: Once a ministerial clerk named Bao Hui came to Donghai on business and called at Wang Liang's house; Wang Liang's wife was dragging firewood home from the fields in a homespun skirt.
units.literal: At that time a clerk of the Minister of Education, Bao Hui, on business came to Donghai, passed to inquire at his home, and Liang's wife in cloth skirt was dragging firewood and returned from the fields.

units.zh: 恢告曰：『我司徒史也，故來受書，欲見夫人。』
units.en: Bao Hui announced himself: 'I am a clerk of the minister of education, here to collect papers—I should like to see your mistress.'
units.literal: Hui announced, saying, 'I am a clerk of the Minister of Education; I have come to receive documents and wish to see the lady.'

units.zh: 妻曰：『妾是也。
units.en: She replied, 'I am the woman of the house.'
units.literal: The wife said, 'Your handmaid is she.'

units.zh: 若掾，無書。』
units.en: But, sir, there are no papers here.'
units.literal: Sir clerk, there are no documents.'

units.zh: 恢乃下拜，嘆息而還，聞者莫不嘉之。
units.en: Bao Hui bowed low, sighed, and withdrew; everyone who heard the story praised her.
units.literal: Hui thereupon descended and bowed, sighed and returned; those who heard were without exception praising it.

units.zh: 後以病歸，一歲復征，至滎陽，疾篤不任進道，乃過其友人。
units.en: Later he went home on sick leave; a year later he was summoned again, but at Xingyang he was too ill to travel on and stopped with a friend.
units.literal: Later citing illness he returned home; after one year he was again summoned; when he reached Xingyang, his illness was grave and he could not undertake to advance on the road, and he passed by his friend.

units.zh: 友人不肯見，曰：『不有忠言奇謀而取大位，何其往來屑屑不憚煩也？』
units.en: The friend refused to receive him, saying, 'You reached high rank without a single memorable counsel—why do you keep shuttling back and forth so busily?'
units.literal: The friend was unwilling to see him and said, 'Without loyal words or strange stratagems you took a great position—how is it that you come and go fussily and do not tire of the trouble?'

units.zh: 遂拒之。
units.en: He turned Wang Liang away.
units.literal: Thereupon he rejected him.

units.zh: 良慚，自後連征，輒稱病。
units.en: Wang Liang was mortified; from then on every new summons met the excuse of illness.
units.literal: Liang was ashamed; from then on whenever repeatedly summoned, he always claimed illness.

units.zh: 詔以玄纁聘之，遂不應。
units.en: The court sent the formal black-and-red gift bundle to engage him; he still would not answer.
units.literal: An edict used dark silk to hire him; he thereupon did not respond.

units.zh: 後光武幸蘭陵，遣使者問良所苦疾，不能言對。
units.en: Later, when Emperor Guangwu toured Lanling, he sent to ask what ailed Wang Liang; Wang Liang could not bring himself to reply.
units.literal: Later Guangwu visited Lanling and sent an envoy to ask what illness Liang suffered; he could not speak in reply.

units.zh: 詔復其子孫邑中徭役，卒於家。
units.en: An edict exempted his descendants from local corvée; he died at home.
units.literal: An edict remitted corvée labor for his descendants in the village; he died at home.

units.zh: 論曰：夫利仁者或借仁以從利，體義者不期體以合義。
units.en: The historian remarks: Some who speak of humanity only borrow it for gain; those who truly live by duty do not perform duty for show.
units.literal: The disquisition says: Those who profit by benevolence perhaps borrow benevolence to follow profit; those who embody rightness do not expect embodiment in order to match rightness.

units.zh: 季文子妾不衣帛，魯人以為美談。
units.en: Ji Wenzi's concubines wore no silk; the people of Lu praised it as a noble example.
units.literal: Ji Wenzi's concubines did not wear silk; the people of Lu took it as a fine tale.

units.zh: 公孫弘身服布被，汲黯譏其多詐。
units.en: Gongsun Hong affected a cotton quilt while drawing a minister's salary; Ji An called him out for shameless pretense.
units.literal: Gongsun Hong personally wore a cloth quilt; Ji An ridiculed him as greatly deceitful.

units.zh: 事實未殊而譽毀別議。
units.en: The facts were much the same, yet one man was lauded and the other mocked.
units.literal: The facts were not different yet praise and blame were separately debated.

units.zh: 何也？
units.en: Why was that?
units.literal: Why?

units.zh: 將體之與利之異乎？
units.en: Is there a difference between living a principle and merely profiting from its reputation?
units.literal: Is embodying it different from profiting by it?

units.zh: 宣秉、王良處位優重，而秉甘疏薄，良妻荷薪，可謂行過乎儉。
units.en: Xuan Bing and Wang Liang held exalted posts, yet Xuan Bing embraced the barest living and Wang Liang's wife hauled firewood home—both carried austerity past what the world expected.
units.literal: Xuan Bing and Wang Liang occupied positions that were honored and weighty, yet Bing was willing to be sparse and thin, and Liang's wife carried firewood—one may say their conduct exceeded in frugality.

units.zh: 然當世咨其清，人君高其節，豈非臨之以誠哉！
units.en: Still their contemporaries praised their purity, and their sovereigns honored their integrity—surely because genuine virtue commands respect!
units.literal: Yet the age consulted on their purity, and rulers of men esteemed their integrity—was it not because they were faced with sincerity!

units.zh: 語曰：『同言而信，則信在言前；
units.en: The proverb runs: "When people already trust you, your word arrives with credit to spare;
units.literal: A saying states, "When the same words are trusted, then trust lies before the words;

units.zh: 同令而行，則誠在令外。』
units.en: when they obey your commands without hesitation, your good faith has already passed beyond the written order."
units.literal: when the same orders are carried out, then sincerity lies beyond the orders."

units.zh: 不其然乎！
units.en: Is that not exactly how it works!
units.literal: Is it not so!

units.zh: 張湛不屑矜偽之誚，斯不偽矣。
units.en: Zhang Zhan brushed off charges of affectation, and in doing so proved he was not posing.
units.literal: Zhang Zhan disdained to mind the ridicule of affected pretense—thus he was not pretentious.

units.zh: 王丹難於交執之道，斯知交矣。
units.en: Wang Dan treated friendship as a grave trust—so he truly understood what friendship costs.
units.literal: Wang Dan found difficult the way of holding fast in friendship—thus he knew friendship.

units.zh: 杜林字伯山，扶風茂陵人也。
units.en: Du Lin, styled Boshan, came from Maoling in Fufeng.
units.literal: Du Lin, courtesy name Boshan, was a man of Maoling in Fufeng commandery.

units.zh: 父鄴，成、哀間為涼州刺史。
units.en: His father Du Ye served as inspector of Liang province under Emperors Cheng and Ai.
units.literal: His father Ye, between Cheng and Ai, was Inspector of Liang province.

units.zh: 林少好學沈深，家既多書，又外氏張竦父子喜文采，林從竦受學，博洽多聞，時稱通儒。
units.en: Du Lin loved learning from boyhood and had a reflective cast of mind; his family owned a large library, and his maternal relatives Zhang Song and son delighted in belles lettres—Du Lin studied under Zhang Song, became encyclopedic in learning, and his generation hailed him as a consummate scholar.
units.literal: Lin in youth was fond of learning and profound; the household already had many books, and moreover his mother's kin Zhang Song and his son were fond of literary polish; Lin received instruction from Song, was broadly learned and heard much, and the age called him a thorough Confucian.

units.zh: 初為郡吏。
units.en: He began as a commandery clerk.
units.literal: At first he was a clerk of the commandery.

units.zh: 王莽敗，盜賊起，林與弟成及同郡範逡、孟冀等，將細弱俱客河西。
units.en: When Wang Mang fell and banditry flared, Du Lin fled west of the Yellow River with his brother Du Cheng, Fan Qun, Meng Ji, and others from the commandery, taking women and children along.
units.literal: When Wang Mang fell, bandits arose; Lin together with his younger brother Cheng and Fan Qun, Meng Ji, and others of the same commandery led the women and children and together sojourned west of the River.

units.zh: 道逢賊數千人，遂掠取財裝，褫奪衣服，拔刃向林等將欲殺之。
units.en: They met several thousand brigands who robbed them bare, stripped their clothes, and leveled swords as if to slaughter them all.
units.literal: On the road they encountered several thousand bandits, who thereupon plundered their goods and baggage, stripped their clothing, drew blades toward Lin and the others and were about to kill them.

units.zh: 冀仰曰：『願一言而死。
units.en: Meng Ji looked up and said, 'Let me speak one sentence before I die.'
units.literal: Ji looked up and said, 'I wish one word and then to die.'

units.zh: 將軍知天神乎？
units.en: General, do you know how Heaven judges men?
units.literal: General, do you understand the spirits of Heaven?

units.zh: 赤眉兵眾百萬，所向無前，而殘賊不道，卒至破敗。
units.en: The Red Eyebrows mustered a million men and swept all before them, yet their cruelty and lawlessness brought them to ruin in the end.
units.literal: The Red Eyebrows had troops in the millions, wherever they went none stood before them, yet they were cruel bandits without the Way, and in the end arrived at defeat and destruction.

units.zh: 今將軍以數千之眾，欲規霸王之事，不行仁恩而反遵覆車，不畏天乎？』
units.en: You command only a few thousand yet dream of hegemony; instead of kindness you repeat the mistake of those who fell before—do you not fear Heaven's anger?"
units.literal: Now the general, with a host of only several thousand, wishes to plan the affairs of a hegemon-king; you do not practice benevolence and favor but on the contrary follow the overturned cart—do you not fear Heaven?"

units.zh: 賊遂釋之，俱免於難。
units.en: The bandits let them go, and the whole party walked free.
units.literal: The bandits thereupon released them, and all were spared from disaster.

units.zh: 隗囂素聞林誌節，深相敬待，以為持書平。
units.en: Wei Ao, who had long admired Du Lin's integrity, received him with great respect and named him examining clerk for palace documents.
units.literal: Wei Ao had long heard of Lin's purpose and integrity, treated him with deep respect, and appointed him examining clerk for palace documents.

units.zh: 後因疾告去，辭還祿食。
units.en: Later he asked leave on grounds of illness, resigned his stipend, and returned his grain allowance.
units.literal: Later citing illness he requested to depart, declined and returned salary and rations.

units.zh: 囂復欲令強起，遂稱篤。
units.en: When Wei Ao tried to force him back to office, Du Lin pleaded a mortal illness.
units.literal: Ao again wished to make him forcibly rise, and he thereupon claimed grave illness.

units.zh: 囂意雖相望，且欲優容之，乃出令曰：『杜伯山天子所不能臣，諸侯所不能友，蓋伯夷、叔齊恥食周粟。
units.en: Wei Ao still wanted his service yet meant to indulge him, and issued a proclamation: 'Du Boshan cannot be bound as a subject to the Son of Heaven nor kept as a friend by any prince—he is another Boyi and Shuqi, ashamed to eat the grain of Zhou.'
units.literal: Ao's mind though still looked to him, and moreover wished to treat him with generous tolerance, thereupon issued an order saying, 'Du Boshan is one whom the Son of Heaven could not make his subject, whom the feudal lords could not make his friend—he is like Boyi and Shuqi, who were ashamed to eat Zhou grain.

units.zh: 今且從師友之位，須道開通，使順所誌。』
units.en: For the present treat him as mentor and companion; when the road is clear again, let him follow his own resolve.'
units.literal: For now let him occupy the place of teacher-friend; wait until the Way is open and unobstructed, and cause him to follow what he purposes.'

units.zh: 林雖拘於囂，而終不屈節。
units.en: Though Wei Ao held him fast, Du Lin never compromised his principles.
units.literal: Although Lin was detained by Ao, to the end he did not bend his integrity.

units.zh: 建武六年，弟成物故，囂乃聽林持喪東歸。
units.en: In Jianwu 6 his brother Du Cheng died; Wei Ao finally allowed Du Lin to escort the body home to the east.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Jianwu, his younger brother Cheng died; Ao then permitted Lin to hold mourning and return east.

units.zh: 既遣而悔，追令刺客楊賢於隴坻遮殺之。
units.en: He regretted the decision as soon as Du Lin left and sent the assassin Yang Xian to waylay and murder him at Long Slope.
units.literal: After dispatching him he regretted it, and pursued with orders for the assassin Yang Xian to intercept and kill him at Longdi.

units.zh: 賢見林身推鹿車，載致弟喪，乃嘆曰：『當今之世，誰能行義？
units.en: Yang Xian found Du Lin alone, pushing a handcart loaded with his brother's coffin, and sighed, 'In times like these, who still keeps faith with duty?
units.literal: Xian saw Lin personally pushing a deer cart, bearing his younger brother's funeral, and sighed, saying, 'In the present age, who can practice righteousness?

units.zh: 我雖小人，何忍殺義士！』
units.en: I am a common fellow, yet how could I strike down a man of honor!'
units.literal: I, though a petty man, how could I bear to kill a man of righteousness!'

units.zh: 因亡去。
units.en: With that he slipped away and left the job undone.
units.literal: Thereupon he fled away.

units.zh: 光武聞林已還三輔，乃征拜侍禦史，引見，問以經書故舊及西州事，甚悅之，賜車馬衣被。
units.en: Learning that Du Lin had reached the capital region, Emperor Guangwu summoned him as attendant censor, received him in audience, questioned him on the classics, old friends, and the western frontier, took great pleasure in his answers, and showered him with carriages, horses, and fine clothes.
units.literal: When Guangwu heard that Lin had already returned to the Three Adjuncts, he thereupon summoned and appointed him Attendant Imperial Clerk, introduced him in audience, asked him about the classics, old affairs, and matters of the western provinces, was very pleased with him, and bestowed carriage, horses, clothing, and bedding.

units.zh: 群寮知林以名德用，甚尊憚之。
units.en: The whole bureaucracy knew he had been chosen for character as much as learning, and treated him with awe.
units.literal: The host of officials knew Lin was employed for name and virtue, and greatly revered and feared him.

units.zh: 京師士大夫，鹹推其博洽。
units.en: Every scholar-official at court extolled his erudition.
units.literal: The gentlemen grandees of the capital all praised his broad learning.

units.zh: 河南鄭興、東海衛宏等，皆長於古學。
units.en: Zheng Xing of Henan, Wei Hong of Donghai, and their circle excelled in classical scholarship.
units.literal: Zheng Xing of Henan, Wei Hong of Donghai, and others were all long in ancient learning.

units.zh: 興嘗師事劉歆，林既遇之，欣然言曰：『林得興等固諧矣，使宏得林，且有以益之。』
units.en: Zheng Xing had studied under Liu Xin; when Du Lin met him he exclaimed, 'To win colleagues like Zheng Xing is harmony enough for me; were Wei Hong to study with me, he would gain still more.'
units.literal: Xing had once taken Liu Xin as his teacher; when Lin encountered him, he happily said, 'For Lin to obtain Xing and the like is indeed harmony; if Hong could obtain Lin, there would yet be something by which to enrich him.'

units.zh: 及宏見林，闇然而服。
units.en: When Wei Hong met Du Lin he fell silent, utterly won over.
units.literal: When Hong saw Lin, he was silent and submitted.

units.zh: 濟南徐巡，始師事宏，後皆更受林學。
units.en: Xu Xun of Jinan had first studied under Wei Hong; both men then sat at Du Lin's feet for further instruction.
units.literal: Xu Xun of Jinan at first served Hong as teacher; afterward both received Lin's learning anew.

units.zh: 林前於西州得漆書《古文尚書》一卷，常寶愛之，雖遭難困，握持不離身。
units.en: In the west Du Lin had acquired a single lacquer-ink manuscript of the Old Text Book of Documents, which he cherished through every hardship and never let leave his side.
units.literal: Lin earlier in the western provinces had obtained one scroll of lacquer-ink text of the Old Text Documents; he constantly treasured and loved it; although he encountered hardship and distress, he grasped and held it and did not leave his person.

units.zh: 出以示宏等曰：『林流離兵亂，常恐斯經將絕。
units.en: He showed it to Wei Hong and the rest, saying, 'I wandered through war and always feared this text would perish with me.'
units.literal: He brought it out to show Hong and the others, saying, 'Lin wandered in military chaos and always feared this classic would be cut off.'

units.zh: 何意東海衛子、濟南徐生復能傳之，是道竟不墜於地也。
units.en: Who would have thought Wei Zi of Donghai and Xu Sheng of Jinan would take it up again—so the teaching never touched the earth.'
units.literal: Who would have thought that Wei Zi of Donghai and Xu Sheng of Jinan could again transmit it—thus the Way in the end did not fall to the ground.'

units.zh: 古文雖不合時務，然願諸生無悔所學。』
units.en: The old-text version may not suit current politics, yet I urge you not to regret the learning you have won.'
units.literal: The old text though does not suit present affairs, yet I wish you gentlemen not to regret what you have studied.'

units.zh: 宏、巡益重之，於是古文遂行。
units.en: Wei Hong and Xu Xun prized him all the more, and the Old Text school spread from that moment.
units.literal: Hong and Xun increasingly esteemed him; thereupon the old text circulated.

units.zh: 明年，大議郊祀制，多以為周郊後稷，漢當祀堯。
units.en: The next year the court debated suburban sacrifice: most argued that since the Zhou honored Hou Ji at the outer altars, Han should honor Yao.
units.literal: The next year, in the great deliberation on suburban sacrifice regulations, most held that Zhou sacrificed to Hou Ji at the suburbs, and Han ought to sacrifice to Yao.

units.zh: 詔復下公卿議，議者僉同，帝亦然之。
units.en: The emperor referred the matter again to the high ministers, who agreed unanimously, and he was inclined to follow them.
units.literal: An edict again sent it down to the dukes and ministers for deliberation; the deliberators were all in agreement, and the emperor also approved it.

units.zh: 林獨以為周室之興，祚由後稷，漢業特起，功不緣堯。
units.en: Du Lin alone argued that Zhou rose through the virtue of Hou Ji, whereas Han's mandate sprang from its own founders, not from Yao's line.
units.literal: Lin alone held that the rise of the Zhou house, its blessing came from Hou Ji; the Han enterprise arose especially, its merit did not follow from Yao.

units.zh: 祖宗故事，所宜因循。
units.en: The ancestral precedents of the dynasty should be kept as they stand.
units.literal: The precedents of forefathers and ancestors are what ought to be followed and continued.

units.zh: 定從林議。
units.en: The court settled on Du Lin's view.
units.literal: The decision followed Lin's proposal.

units.zh: 後代王良為大司徒司直。
units.en: He later succeeded Wang Liang as grandee of the grand minister of education for directorships.
units.literal: Later he replaced Wang Liang as Grandee of the Grand Minister of Education for Directorships.

units.zh: 林薦同郡範逡、趙秉、申屠剛及隴西牛邯等，皆被擢用，士多歸之。
units.en: He recommended Fan Qun, Zhao Bing, Shentu Gang, Niu Han of Longxi, and others; each won appointment, and talent flocked to his banner.
units.literal: Lin recommended Fan Qun, Zhao Bing, Shen Tu Gang, and Niu Han of Longxi, and others of the same sort; all were promoted and employed, and many scholars attached to him.

units.zh: 十一年，司直官罷，以林代郭憲為光祿勛。
units.en: In the eleventh year the directorship post was abolished, and Du Lin replaced Guo Xian as bearer of the brightness.
units.literal: In the eleventh year, the office of grandee for directorships was abolished, and Lin replaced Guo Xian as Bearer of the Brightness.

units.zh: 內奉宿衛，外總三署，周密敬慎，選舉稱平。
units.en: Within the palace he stood night watch; outside he superintended the three cadet bureaus; he was meticulous and even-handed in appointments.
units.literal: Within he attended night guard; without he oversaw the three bureaus; he was thorough, careful, and respectful, and in selection and promotion he was called even.

units.zh: 郎有好學者，輒見誘進，朝夕滿堂。
units.en: Whenever a gentleman cadet showed scholarly promise, Du Lin drew him forward until his hall teemed with students morning and night.
units.literal: When gentlemen cadets were fond of learning, he always saw them enticed forward; morning and evening the hall was full.

units.zh: 十四年，群臣上言：『古者肉刑嚴重，則人畏法令；
units.en: In the fourteenth year ministers memorialized: 'Under the ancients harsh mutilation made the people dread the law;
units.literal: In the fourteenth year, the host of ministers submitted words, saying, 'In antiquity corporal punishment was severe, then the people feared laws and orders;

units.zh: 今憲律輕薄，故奸軌不勝。
units.en: today our code is so mild that crime runs beyond control.'
units.literal: now statutes and ordinances are light and thin, therefore treachery and villainy cannot be overcome.'

units.zh: 宜增科禁，以防其源。』
units.en: We should tighten the statutes at the root to choke off wrongdoing.'
units.literal: It is fitting to increase statutes and prohibitions, in order to guard its source.'

units.zh: 詔下公卿。
units.en: The emperor referred the proposal to his ministers.
units.literal: An edict sent it down to the dukes and ministers.

units.zh: 林奏曰：『夫人情挫辱，則義節之風損，法防繁多，則敬免之行興。
units.en: Du Lin answered with a memorial: 'When the law humiliates ordinary feelings, honor withers; when statutes multiply, people learn only to dodge punishment.
units.literal: Lin memorialized, saying, 'As for human feelings, when they are humiliated and insulted, then the wind of righteousness and integrity is damaged; when legal safeguards are numerous, then conduct of mere evasion of punishment arises.

units.zh: 孔子曰：「導之以政，齊之以刑，民免而無恥。
units.en: Confucius said, "If you herd the people with edicts and lash them with penalties, they will keep out of trouble but lose all sense of shame.
units.literal: Confucius said, "Lead them with administrative measures and regulate them with punishments, and the people will evade but have no sense of shame.

units.zh: 導之以德，齊之以禮，有恥且格。」
units.en: Lead them with virtue and restrain them with ritual, and they will feel shame and set themselves right."
units.literal: Lead them with virtue and regulate them with ritual, and they will have a sense of shame and moreover will correct themselves."

units.zh: 古之明王，深識遠慮，動居其厚，不務多辟，周之五刑，不過三千。
units.en: The wise kings of old looked far ahead and acted with generous restraint, never multiplying executions: even Zhou's five punishments numbered fewer than three thousand clauses.'
units.literal: The enlightened kings of antiquity, with deep knowledge and far planning, in action dwelt in the thick and did not strive for many punishments; the five punishments of Zhou did not exceed three thousand.'

units.zh: 大漢初興，詳鑒失得，故破矩為圓，斫雕為樸，蠲除苛政，更立疏網，海內歡欣，人懷寬德。
units.en: When Han first rose it weighed past mistakes, rounded harsh corners into mercy, stripped ornament down to simplicity, swept away cruel edicts, and cast a wider net—so the realm rejoiced and the people felt the ruler's kindness.
units.literal: At the first rise of Great Han, it examined in detail loss and gain; therefore it broke the square to make round, hewed carving to make plain, abolished harsh government, and established anew a loose net; within the seas there was joy, and people cherished generous virtue.

units.zh: 及至其後，漸以滋章，吹毛索疵，詆欺無限。
units.en: Later ages piled statute upon statute, hunting for fault in every hairbreadth, until slander and spite knew no limit.
units.literal: When it reached afterward, gradually it became luxuriant; blowing hair to seek flaws, slander and deceit without limit.

units.zh: 果桃菜茹之饋，集以成臧，小事無妨於義，以為大戮，故國無廉士，家無完行。
units.en: A gift of fruit or greens could be tallied into a theft charge; trivial acts that touched no moral core were punished like capital crimes—so honest men vanished from public life and no household kept an unstained name.
units.literal: Gifts of fruit, peaches, and vegetables, gathered to constitute theft; small matters without harm to righteousness, taken as great execution—therefore the state had no incorrupt scholars, and families had no complete conduct.

units.zh: 至於法不能禁，令不能止，上下相遁。
units.en: When law cannot hold what it bans and decrees cannot stop what they forbid, ruler and ruled simply dodge one another.
units.literal: As for law being unable to prohibit and orders being unable to stop, high and low evade one another.

units.zh: 為敝彌深。
units.en: The harm only deepens.
units.literal: The harm done becomes ever deeper.

units.zh: 臣愚以為宜如舊制，不合翻移。』
units.en: I humbly urge that we keep the founding statutes and not overturn them now.'
units.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks it is fitting to follow the old system and not fit to overturn and shift.'

units.zh: 帝從之。
units.en: The emperor accepted his advice.
units.literal: The emperor followed it.

units.zh: 後皇太子彊求乞自退，封東海王，故重選官屬，以林為王傅。
units.en: When Crown Prince Liu Qiang asked to step down and was enfeoffed as king of Donghai, the court refilled his household staff and named Du Lin his tutor.
units.literal: Later the crown prince Qiang requested to beg to retire of himself, was enfeoffed as king of Donghai, and therefore officials were anew heavily selected; Lin was made royal tutor to the king.

units.zh: 從駕南巡狩。
units.en: He accompanied the emperor on a southern inspection tour.
units.literal: He followed the imperial carriage on southern tour and hunt.

units.zh: 時諸王傅數被引命，或多交遊，不得應詔；
units.en: Royal tutors were often summoned on short notice, yet many were off socializing and missed the call;
units.literal: At that time the royal tutors were repeatedly summoned and ordered, or many had social engagements and could not answer the edict;

units.zh: 唯林守慎，有召必至。
units.en: only Du Lin stayed watchful and answered every summons.
units.literal: only Lin kept cautious vigilance; whenever summoned he always arrived.

units.zh: 餘人雖不見譴，而林特受賞賜，又辭不敢受，帝益重之。
units.en: The rest were not punished, but Du Lin alone received imperial largesse—which he declined—so the emperor prized him all the more.
units.literal: Though the others were not seen to be rebuked, yet Lin alone received rewards and gifts, and moreover declined and did not dare accept them; the emperor increasingly esteemed him.

units.zh: 明年，代丁恭為少府。
units.en: The following year he succeeded Ding Gong as privy treasurer.
units.literal: The next year, he replaced Ding Gong as Privy Treasurer.

units.zh: 二十二年，復為光祿勛。
units.en: In the twenty-second year he was again appointed bearer of the brightness.
units.literal: In the twenty-second year, he again became Bearer of the Brightness.

units.zh: 頃之，代朱浮為大司空。
units.en: Soon after he replaced Zhu Fu as grand minister of works.
units.literal: Before long, he replaced Zhu Fu as Grand Minister of Works.

units.zh: 博雅多通，稱為任職相。
units.en: Learned, polished, and versatile, he was hailed as a minister of works who truly filled the role.
units.literal: He was broad, elegant, and broadly conversant, and was called a minister of works equal to the task.

units.zh: 明年薨，帝親自臨喪送葬，除子喬為郎。
units.en: He died the next year; the emperor attended his obsequies in person and appointed his son Du Qiao a gentleman cadet.
units.literal: The next year he died; the emperor personally attended the mourning and sent off the funeral, and appointed his son Qiao Gentleman.

units.zh: 詔曰：『公侯子孫，必復其始，賢者之後，宜宰城邑。
units.en: An edict read, 'The sons of nobles must return to their roots, and a sage's heir should rule a county seat.
units.literal: An edict stated, 'The descendants of dukes and marquises must return to their beginnings; after the worthy, it is fitting to govern cities and towns.

units.zh: 其以喬為丹水長。』
units.en: Let Du Qiao be named chief of Danshui.'
units.literal: Let Qiao be made chief of Danshui.'

units.zh: 論曰：夫威強以自禦，力損則身危；
units.en: The historian remarks: lean on force alone to guard yourself, and when strength fails you stand in peril;
units.literal: The disquisition says: By might and strength to defend oneself—when strength is exhausted then the body is in peril;

units.zh: 飾詐以圖己，詐窮則道屈；
units.en: dress up fraud to serve your ends, and when the mask slips your purpose is broken;
units.literal: by adornment and deceit to scheme for oneself—when deceit is exhausted then the Way is bent;

units.zh: 而忠信篤敬，蠻貊行焉者，誠以德之感物厚矣。
units.en: yet loyalty, good faith, and reverence move even barbarians, for nothing sways others like genuine virtue.
units.literal: yet loyalty, trustworthiness, earnestness, and respect—even the Man and Mo will practice them—indeed it is because sincerity's moving of things is thick.

units.zh: 故趙孟懷忠，匹夫成其仁；
units.en: Thus Zhao Meng clung to good faith and a commoner could accomplish humanity;
units.literal: Therefore Zhao Meng cherished loyalty, and a common man completed his benevolence;

units.zh: 杜林行義，烈士假其命。
units.en: Du Lin lived by duty, and a desperate man spared his life for it.
units.literal: Du Lin practiced righteousness, and a man of fierce resolve borrowed his life.

units.zh: 《易》曰：『人之所助者信』，有不誣矣。
units.en: The Book of Changes says, 'What people help is trustworthiness'—and there is no falsehood in this.
units.literal: The Changes states, 'What men help is trustworthiness'—there is no falsehood in this.'

units.zh: 郭丹字少卿，南陽穰人也。
units.en: Guo Dan, styled Shaoqing, was from Rang in Nanyang.
units.literal: Guo Dan, courtesy name Shaoqing, was a man of Rang in Nanyang commandery.

units.zh: 父稚，成帝時為廬江太守，有清名。
units.en: His father Guo Zhi served as grand administrator of Lujiang under Emperor Cheng and was famed for integrity.
units.literal: His father Zhi, in the time of Chengdi, was grand administrator of Lujiang and had a pure reputation.

units.zh: 丹七歲而孤，小心孝順，後母哀憐之，為鬻衣裝，買產業。
units.en: Guo Dan lost his father at seven; he was dutiful and careful, so his stepmother pitied him, sold her ornaments, and bought him land and goods.
units.literal: Dan at seven sui was orphaned; he was careful and filial; the stepmother pitied him and for him sold clothing and gear and bought property.

units.zh: 後從師長安，買符入函谷關，乃慨然嘆曰：『丹不乘使者車，終不出關。』
units.en: Later he studied in Chang'an; when he bought his pass to enter Hangu Gate he swore, 'If I do not ride out as an imperial envoy, I will not cross this barrier again.'
units.literal: Later he followed a teacher to Chang'an; buying a tally he entered Hangu Pass, and thereupon sighed with feeling, saying, 'Dan, if I do not ride an envoy's carriage, in the end I will not leave the pass.'

units.zh: 既至京師，常為都講，諸儒鹹敬重之。
units.en: In the capital he regularly served as chief lecturer, and the scholars held him in high regard.
units.literal: When he had reached the capital, he constantly was chief lecturer, and the various Confucians all respected him.

units.zh: 大司馬嚴尤請丹，辭病不就。
units.en: Grand Marshal Yan You summoned him, but he pleaded illness and stayed away.
units.literal: Grand Marshal Yan You invited Dan; he declined illness and did not take up the post.

units.zh: 王莽又征之，遂與諸生逃於北地。
units.en: Wang Mang summoned him again, so he fled north into Beidi with a band of students.
units.literal: Wang Mang again summoned him; he thereupon with various students fled to Beidi.

units.zh: 更始二年，三公舉丹賢能，征為諫議大夫，持節使歸南陽，安集受降。
units.en: In Gengshi 2 the three excellencies nominated him as worthy and able; he was called to be grandee remonstrant, given credentials, and sent south to Nanyang to pacify the people and receive surrenders.
units.literal: In the second year of Gengshi, the Three Dukes recommended Dan as worthy and able; he was summoned to be Grandee Remonstrant, bearing credentials was sent to return to Nanyang, to pacify and gather those who surrendered.

units.zh: 丹自去家十有二年，果乘高車出關，如其誌焉。
units.en: Twelve years after leaving home he did ride a tall carriage out through the pass, exactly as he had vowed.
units.literal: Dan himself had left home twelve years; in the end he rode a high carriage out of the pass, as his purpose had been.

units.zh: 更始敗，諸將悉歸光武，並獲封爵；
units.en: When the Gengshi regime collapsed, every general rushed to Emperor Guangwu and won titles;
units.literal: When Gengshi fell, the various generals all returned to Guangwu and together received enfeoffments and noble ranks;

units.zh: 丹獨保平氏不下，為更始發喪，衰绖盡哀。
units.en: Guo Dan alone held Pingshi against surrender, then mourned the Gengshi Emperor in full sackcloth.
units.literal: Dan alone kept Pingshi from submitting, for Gengshi held mourning, wearing mourning headband and belt to exhaust grief.

units.zh: 建武二年，遂潛逃去，敝衣間行，涉歷險阻，求謁更始妻子，奉還節傳，因歸鄉裏。
units.en: In Jianwu 2 he slipped away in rags by back roads, braved every danger, found the Gengshi emperor's family, returned his official seals, and made his way home.
units.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, he thereupon secretly fled away, in worn clothing traveled by byways, crossed and experienced peril and obstruction, sought audience with Gengshi's wife and children, presented and returned credentials and tallies, and thereupon returned to his village.

units.zh: 太守杜詩請為功曹，丹薦鄉人長者自代而去。
units.en: Grand Administrator Du Shi offered him the post of merit assessor; Guo Dan named a respected townsman to replace him and left.
units.literal: Grand Administrator Du Shi invited him to be merit assessor; Dan recommended an elder of the village in his place and departed.

units.zh: 詩乃嘆曰：『昔明王興化，卿士讓位，今功曹推賢，可謂至德。
units.en: Du Shi sighed, 'When enlightened kings reformed the realm, high ministers yielded rank; today a merit assessor yields his seat to a better man—that is consummate virtue.
units.literal: Shi thereupon sighed, saying, 'In antiquity when enlightened kings transformed customs, ministers yielded place; now the merit assessor pushes forward the worthy—this can be called utmost virtue.

units.zh: 敕以丹事編署黃堂，以為後法。』
units.en: Inscribe Guo Dan's deed on the Yellow Hall as a precedent for the future.'
units.literal: Order that Dan's affair be compiled and posted on the Yellow Hall, to be a model for later.'

units.zh: 十三年，大司馬吳漢辟舉高第，再遷並州牧，有清平稱。
units.en: In the thirteenth year Grand Marshal Wu Han nominated him top of the list; after two promotions he became governor of Bingzhou, famed for an even and incorrupt administration.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year, Grand Marshal Wu Han recommended him in the highest grade; he was twice transferred to Governor of Bing province and had a reputation for purity and fairness.

units.zh: 轉使匈奴中郎將，遷左馮翊。
units.en: He moved on to serve as general of the household in charge of the Xiongnu envoys, then became left administrator of Fengyi.
units.literal: He was transferred to General of the Household Gentlemen in Charge of the Xiongnu, then transferred to left Administrator of Fengyi.

units.zh: 永平三年，代李訢為司徒。
units.en: In Yongping 3 he succeeded Li Xin as minister of education.
units.literal: In the third year of Yongping, he replaced Li Xin as Minister of Education.

units.zh: 在朝廉直公正，與侯霸、杜林、張湛、郭伋齊名相善。
units.en: At court he was known for integrity and even-handed justice, and stood on the same footing as Hou Ba, Du Lin, Zhang Zhan, and Guo Ji.
units.literal: At court he was incorrupt, straight, and fair, and with Hou Ba, Du Lin, Zhang Zhan, and Guo Ji he shared a name and was on good terms.

units.zh: 明年，坐考隴西太守鄧融事無所據，策免。
units.en: The next year he lost his post for pressing a case against Deng Rong, grand administrator of Longxi, without evidence.
units.literal: The next year, for sitting in judgment on the affair of grand administrator Deng Rong of Longxi without basis, he was dismissed by rescript.

units.zh: 五年，卒於家，時年八十七。
units.en: He died at home in the fifth year, at the age of eighty-seven.
units.literal: In the fifth year, he died at home, aged eighty-seven.

units.zh: 以河南尹範遷有清行，代為司徒。
units.en: Fan Qian of Henan, noted for clean living, was named minister of education in his place.
units.literal: Because Fan Qian, metropolitan governor of Henan, had pure conduct, he replaced him as Minister of Education.

units.zh: 遷字子廬，沛國人，初為漁陽太守，以智略安邊，匈奴不敢入界。
units.en: Fan Qian, styled Zilu, came from the princedom of Pei. As grand administrator of Yuyang he secured the frontier by shrewd policy, and the Xiongnu would not cross his border.
units.literal: Qian, courtesy name Zilu, was a man of the Principality of Pei; at first he was grand administrator of Yuyang, and by strategy and planning he pacified the border, so the Xiongnu did not dare enter his territory.

units.zh: 及在公輔，有宅數畝，田不過一頃，復推與兄子。
units.en: Even as one of the chief ministers he owned only a few mu of house and less than one qing of land, which he then signed over to his nephew.
units.literal: When among the highest ministers, he had a residence of several mu and fields not exceeding one qing, yet again he pushed them to his elder brother's son.

units.zh: 其妻嘗謂曰：『君有四子而無立錐之地，可余奉祿，以為後世業。』
units.en: His wife once said, 'You have four sons and not a handspan of soil—why not salt away your salary for their future.'
units.literal: His wife once said to him, 'You have four sons yet not land to stick an awl; you could set aside your salary to build an estate for posterity.'

units.zh: 遷曰：『吾備位大臣而蓄財求利，何以示後世！』
units.en: Fan Qian replied, 'I sit among the great ministers; if I piled up silver for my heirs, what example would I leave!'
units.literal: Qian said, 'I occupy a minister's place yet hoard wealth and seek profit—how would I show posterity!'

units.zh: 在位四年薨，家無擔石焉。
units.en: He died in office after four years, leaving his household without a peck to spare.
units.literal: After four years in office he died; the family had not a dan or shi of grain.

units.zh: 後顯宗因朝會問群臣：『郭丹家今何如？』
units.en: Later Emperor Ming asked his ministers at audience, 'What has become of Guo Dan's family?'
units.literal: Later, at court assembly, Emperor Xianzong asked the host of ministers, 'How is Guo Dan's family now?'

units.zh: 宗正劉匡對曰：『昔孫叔敖相楚，馬不秣粟，妻不衣帛，子孫竟蒙寢丘之封。
units.en: Liu Kuang, director of the imperial clan, answered, 'Sunshu Ao served Chu with such austerity that his horses ate no grain and his wife wore no silk, yet his line still won the fief of Qiuqiu.'
units.literal: Director of the Imperial Clan Liu Kuang replied, 'In the past Sunshu Ao was minister of Chu: his horses were not fed grain, his wife did not wear silk, yet in the end his descendants received the fief of Qiuqiu.'

units.zh: 丹出典州郡，入為三公，而家無遺產，子孫困匱。』
units.en: Guo Dan rose from provincial posts to the three excellencies, yet died without an estate; his descendants were left destitute."
units.literal: Dan went out to govern provinces and commanderies and entered as one of the Three Dukes, yet his house had no leftover property, and sons and grandsons were in want."

units.zh: 帝乃下南陽訪求其嗣。
units.en: The emperor then commanded Nanyang to seek out his posterity.
units.literal: The emperor thereupon sent orders down to Nanyang to search out his heirs.

units.zh: 長子宇，官至常山太守。
units.en: His eldest son Guo Yu rose to be grand administrator of Changshan.
units.literal: The eldest son Yu, office reached grand administrator of Changshan.

units.zh: 少子濟，趙相。
units.en: His younger son Guo Ji became minister of Zhao.
units.literal: The younger son Ji, minister of Zhao.

units.zh: 吳良字大儀，齊國臨淄人也。
units.en: Wu Liang, styled Dayi, was a native of Linzi in Qi.
units.literal: Wu Liang, courtesy name Dayi, was a man of Linzi in the Principality of Qi.

units.zh: 初為郡吏，歲旦與掾史入賀，門下掾王望舉觴上壽，謅稱太守功德。
units.en: He began as a commandery clerk. On New Year's morning he went in with the staff to pay respects; the porter Wang Wang raised a cup, gushing praise of the grand administrator's achievements.
units.literal: At first he was a clerk of the commandery; on New Year's dawn he entered with the clerks and assistants to congratulate; the gatehouse clerk Wang Wang raised a cup to toast long life, flatteringly praising the grand administrator's merit and virtue.

units.zh: 良於下坐勃然進曰：『望佞邪之人，欺謅無狀，願勿受其觴。』
units.en: From the back row Wu Liang sprang up and said, 'Wang is a sycophant whose praise is empty flattery—do not drink his toast.'
units.literal: Liang from the lower seat suddenly advanced and said, 'Wang is a fawning and evil man who deceives and flatters without restraint; I beg you not to accept his cup.'

units.zh: 太守斂容而止。
units.en: The grand administrator checked himself and set the cup down.
units.literal: The grand administrator composed his countenance and stopped.

units.zh: 宴罷，轉良為功曹；
units.en: When the feast broke up, the governor named Wu Liang merit assessor;
units.literal: When the banquet ended, he transferred Liang to merit assessor;

units.zh: 恥以言受進，終不肯謁。
units.en: but Wu Liang was ashamed to owe the post to flattery and never reported for duty.
units.literal: ashamed to advance by words, to the end he was unwilling to pay formal visit.

units.zh: 時，驃騎將軍東平王蒼聞而辟之，署為西曹。
units.en: General of agile cavalry, Prince Liu Cang of Dongping, heard of him and took him on as a western-bureau clerk.
units.literal: At that time General of Agile Cavalry, Prince Cang of Dongping, heard of it and summoned him, appointing him to the western bureau.

units.zh: 蒼甚相敬受，上疏薦良曰：『臣聞為國所重，必在得人；
units.en: Prince Cang esteemed him deeply and memorialized: 'What a state must prize above all is the right men in office;
units.literal: Cang greatly respected and received him, and submitted a memorial recommending Liang, saying, 'Your servant has heard that what the state esteems must lie in obtaining the right men;

units.zh: 報恩之義，莫大薦士。
units.en: and nothing repays a sovereign's kindness like lifting worthy men to his notice.'
units.literal: in the meaning of repaying favor, nothing is greater than recommending scholars.'

units.zh: 竊見臣府西曹掾齊國吳良，資質敦固，公方廉恪，躬儉安貧，白首一節；
units.en: Your servant's western-bureau clerk Wu Liang of Qi is steadfast by nature, square and scrupulous, content in poverty though gray-haired, unwavering in principle;
units.literal: Your servant has privately observed the western-bureau clerk Wu Liang of Qi in my household: his endowment is honest and firm, he is upright, incorrupt, and reverent, personally frugal and content in poverty, white-haired yet of one integrity;

units.zh: 又治《尚書》，學通師法，經任博士，行中表儀。
units.en: he has mastered the Book of Documents in the orthodox school tradition, is fit to be an erudite, and his deportment is a mirror for others.
units.literal: moreover he has studied the Documents, his learning penetrates the master's methods, he could fill the post of erudite, and in conduct he is a model inside and out.

units.zh: 宜備宿衛，以輔聖政。
units.en: He should join the palace guard to help perfect your government.'
units.literal: It is fitting to assign him to night guard to assist sagely government.'

units.zh: 臣蒼榮寵絕矣，憂責深大，私慕公叔同升之義，懼於臧文竊位之罪，敢秉愚瞽，犯冒嚴禁。』
units.en: I have received more honor than I deserve and a heavier charge than I can bear; privately I admire Gongshu's example of rising together, and I fear the crime of Zang Wen's stealing a place—so I risk your displeasure to speak.'
units.literal: Your servant Cang's glory and favor are already extreme; my burden of responsibility is deep and great; privately I admire Gongshu's meaning of rising together, and fear the crime of Zang Wen's stealing a place; I dare, holding my foolish blindness, to offend against stern prohibitions.'

units.zh: 顯宗以示公卿曰：『前以事見良，須發皓然，衣冠甚偉。
units.en: Emperor Ming showed the memorial to the high ministers, saying, 'I met Wu Liang on business once: his hair was snow-white, his dress magnificent.'
units.literal: Xianzong showed it to the dukes and ministers, saying, 'Earlier I saw Liang on business: his beard and hair were hoary white, his cap and robes very imposing.'

units.zh: 夫薦賢助國，宰相之職，蕭何舉韓信，設壇而拜，不復考試。
units.en: Recommending talent is the chancellor's work: Xiao He raised Han Xin to general on a single ceremony, with no further examination.'
units.literal: To recommend the worthy and assist the state is the duty of the minister of education; Xiao He recommended Han Xin, set up the altar and invested him, without again examining and testing.'

units.zh: 今以良為議郎。』
units.en: Let Wu Liang be appointed gentleman consultant.'
units.literal: Now appoint Liang Gentleman Consultant.'

units.zh: 永平中，車駕近出，而信陽侯陰就幹突禁衛，車府令徐匡鉤就車，收禦者送獄。
units.en: During Yongping the emperor rode out on a short tour; Marquis Yin Jiu of Xinyang forced his way through the palace guard; carriage-house director Xu Kuang seized his chariot and jailed the charioteer.
units.literal: In the Yongping period, the imperial carriage went out on a near excursion, and Marquis of Xinyang Yin Jiu burst through the forbidden guard; the carriage-house director Xu Kuang hooked Jiu's carriage and arrested the driver and sent him to prison.

units.zh: 詔書譴匡，匡乃自系。
units.en: An edict rebuked Xu Kuang, who then placed himself in fetters.
units.literal: An edict rebuked Kuang; Kuang thereupon bound himself.

units.zh: 良上言曰：『信陽侯就倚恃外戚，幹犯乘輿，無人臣禮，為大不敬。
units.en: Wu Liang memorialized: 'Yin Jiu trades on his status as an imperial in-law, obstructs the imperial train, and shows none of a subject's deference—that is grave disrespect.'
units.literal: Liang submitted words, saying, 'Marquis of Xinyang Jiu relies on being maternal kin, violates the imperial equipage, lacks the ritual of minister and subject, and is greatly irreverent.'

units.zh: 匡執法守正，反下於理，臣恐聖化由是而弛。』
units.en: Yet Xu Kuang, who only upheld the law, faces the judge himself—I fear your moral sway will slacken if this stands.'
units.literal: Kuang in holding the law and guarding rectitude is instead sent down to the judicial authorities; your servant fears sagely transformation will thereby slacken.'

units.zh: 帝雖赦匡，猶左轉良為即丘長。
units.en: The emperor pardoned Xu Kuang but still demoted Wu Liang to magistrate of Jiqiu.
units.literal: Although the emperor pardoned Kuang, he still demoted Liang leftward to be chief of Jiqiu.

units.zh: 後遷司徒長史。
units.en: He was later promoted to senior clerk under the minister of education.
units.literal: Later he was transferred to senior clerk of the Minister of Education.

units.zh: 每處大議，輒據經典，不希旨偶俗，以僥時譽。
units.en: In every great debate he cited the classics, never trimming his views to court fashion or chasing cheap applause.
units.literal: Whenever seated in great deliberation, he always relied on the classics, and did not trim to imperial intent or echo vulgar opinion so as to angle for temporary praise.

units.zh: 後坐事免，復拜議郎，卒於官。
units.en: He was later removed over a case, then recalled as gentleman consultant and died in that post.
units.literal: Later for sitting in an affair he was dismissed; again he was appointed Gentleman Consultant and died in office.

units.zh: 承宮字少子，瑯邪姑幕人也。
units.en: Cheng Gong, styled Shaozi, came from Gumu in Langya.
units.literal: Cheng Gong, courtesy name Shaozi, was a man of Gumu in Langya commandery.

units.zh: 少孤，年八歲為人牧豕。
units.en: Orphaned young, at eight he hired out as a swineherd.
units.literal: In youth he was orphaned; at eight sui he herded pigs for people.

units.zh: 鄉裏徐子盛者，以《春秋經》授諸生數百人，宮過息廬下，樂其業，因就聽經，遂請留門下，為諸生拾薪。
units.en: A neighbor, Xu Zisheng, taught the Spring and Autumn Annals to hundreds of pupils. Cheng Gong rested under his eaves, loved what he heard, asked to stay on as fuel-gatherer for the school.
units.literal: In the village there was Xu Zisheng, who with the Spring and Autumn classic instructed several hundred students; Gong passed and rested beneath his hut, delighted with their undertaking, thereupon drew near to listen to the classic, then requested to remain at the gate, gathering firewood for the students.

units.zh: 執苦數年，勤學不倦。
units.en: For years he labored without flagging at his books.
units.literal: He endured hardship several years, studied diligently without weariness.

units.zh: 經典既明，乃歸家教授。
units.en: Once he had mastered the texts he went home to teach on his own.
units.literal: When the classics were already clear, he returned home and taught.

units.zh: 遭天下喪亂，遂將諸生避地漢中，後與妻子之蒙陰山，肆力耕種。
units.en: When chaos swept the realm he led his pupils to refuge in Hanzhong, then moved with his family to Mengyin Mountain and farmed with all his might.
units.literal: Encountering the world's bereavement and disorder, he thereupon led the various students to flee and settle in Hanzhong; later with wife and children he went to Mengyin Mountain and exerted strength in plowing and planting.

units.zh: 禾黍將孰，人有認之者，宮不與計，推之而去，由是顯名。
units.en: As the crop ripened a neighbor claimed the field; Cheng Gong yielded the grain without argument and walked away, and his name spread.
units.literal: When the grain was about to ripen, someone claimed it was his; Gong did not dispute with him, pushed it aside and departed, whereby he became famous.

units.zh: 三府更辟，皆不應。
units.en: The three highest bureaus summoned him in turn; he refused every call.
units.literal: The three offices repeatedly summoned him; all he did not answer.

units.zh: 永平中，征詣公車。
units.en: During the Yongping era he was summoned to the imperial carriage office.
units.literal: During the Yongping era, he was summoned to the Imperial Carriage Office.

units.zh: 車駕臨辟雍，召宮拜博士，遷左中郎將。
units.en: When the emperor attended the Circular Moat, Cheng Gong was summoned, made an erudite, and promoted to left leader of court gentlemen.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage attended the Circular Moat, Gong was summoned and appointed Erudite, then transferred to Left Leader of Court Gentlemen.

units.zh: 數納忠言，陳政，論議切愨，朝臣憚其節，名播匈奴。
units.en: He spoke plainly and often, argued policy with blunt sincerity, and courtiers respected his integrity; his reputation reached the Xiongnu.
units.literal: He repeatedly submitted loyal words, presented policies, and in discussion was earnest and sincere; court ministers feared his integrity, and his name spread among the Xiongnu.

units.zh: 時，北單於遣使求得見宮，顯宗敕自整飾，宮對曰：『夷狄眩名，非識實者也。
units.en: When the northern chanyu asked to meet him, Emperor Ming told Cheng Gong to spruce himself up. Gong answered, "Barbarians chase fame and never see the man behind it.
units.literal: At the time the Northern Chanyu sent envoys asking to see Gong; Emperor Xianzong ordered him to dress himself up. Gong replied, "Barbarians are dazzled by reputation and do not know the reality.

units.zh: 臣狀醜，不可以示遠，宜選有威容者。』
units.en: I am too plain to display to foreigners; choose someone with a more imposing bearing."
units.literal: My appearance is ugly and cannot be shown to distant lands; it is fitting to choose someone with a commanding presence."

units.zh: 帝乃以大鴻臚魏應代之。
units.en: The emperor then sent Grand Herald Wei Ying in his stead.
units.literal: The emperor thereupon had Grand Herald Wei Ying take his place.

units.zh: 十七年，拜侍中祭酒。
units.en: In the seventeenth year he became libationer among palace attendants.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Libationer among Palace Attendants.

units.zh: 建初元年，卒，肅宗褒嘆，賜以冢地。
units.en: He died in Jianchu 1; Emperor Zhang mourned him and granted a burial plot.
units.literal: In the first year of Jianchu he died; Emperor Suzong praised and lamented him and granted a tomb site.

units.zh: 妻上書乞歸葬鄉裏，復賜錢三十萬。
units.en: His wife petitioned to bury him in their home village and received another three hundred thousand cash.
units.literal: His wife submitted a memorial asking to return his body for burial in their home village, and she was additionally granted three hundred thousand cash.

units.zh: 鄭均字仲虞，東平任城人也。
units.en: Zheng Jun, styled Zhongyu, was from Rencheng in Dongping.
units.literal: Zheng Jun, courtesy name Zhongyu, was a man of Rencheng in Dongping commandery.

units.zh: 少好黃、老書。
units.en: In youth he studied the Yellow Emperor and Laozi.
units.literal: In youth he was fond of the books of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi.

units.zh: 兄為縣吏，頗受禮遺，均數諫止，不聽。
units.en: His elder brother served as a county clerk and took bribes; Zheng Jun warned him again and again, without effect.
units.literal: His elder brother was a county clerk and rather received gifts and presents; Jun several times remonstrated to stop him, but he did not listen.

units.zh: 即脫身為傭，歲餘，得錢帛，歸以與兄。
units.en: He hired himself out as a laborer; after a year he brought home coin and silk for his brother.
units.literal: Thereupon he left his person to become a hired laborer; after more than a year he obtained cash and silk, returned and gave them to his elder brother.

units.zh: 曰：『物盡可復得，為吏坐臧，終身捐棄。』
units.en: He said, 'Goods can always be replaced, but a clerk convicted of graft is ruined forever.'
units.literal: He said, 'Things when exhausted can be obtained again; to be a clerk and sit for corruption goods is to be cast off for life.'

units.zh: 兄感其言，遂為廉潔。
units.en: The brother took the lesson to heart and mended his ways.
units.literal: The elder brother was moved by his words and thereupon became incorrupt and clean.

units.zh: 均好義篤實，養寡嫂孤兒，恩禮敦至。
units.en: Zheng Jun loved duty and meant what he said; he supported his widowed sister-in-law and her orphans with unstinting kindness.
units.literal: Jun was fond of righteousness, earnest and solid; he raised his widowed sister-in-law and orphan children, favor and ritual were thick and thorough.

units.zh: 常稱病家廷，不應州郡辟召。
units.en: He habitually pleaded illness at home and ignored every provincial summons.
units.literal: He constantly claimed illness at home in the courtyard, and did not answer province and commandery summons.

units.zh: 郡將欲必致之，使縣令譎將詣門，既至，卒不能屈。
units.en: The regional commander was determined to have him and tricked the county magistrate into delivering him to the yamen gate, yet could not force him to serve.
units.literal: The commandery general wished necessarily to get him and ordered the county magistrate deceitfully to escort him to the gate; when he had arrived, in the end could not bend him.

units.zh: 均於是客於濮陽。
units.en: Zheng Jun then withdrew to live as a guest in Puyang.
units.literal: Jun thereupon sojourned as guest at Puyang.

units.zh: 建初三年，司徒鮑昱辟之，後舉直言，並不詣。
units.en: In Jianchu 3 Minister Bao Yu called for him, and later he was nominated for blunt counsel; he answered neither summons.
units.literal: In the third year of Jianchu, Minister of Education Bao Yu summoned him; later he was recommended for outspoken integrity; both times he did not go.

units.zh: 六年，公車特征。
units.en: In the sixth year the court sent the imperial coach for him alone.
units.literal: In the sixth year, the public carriage specially summoned him.

units.zh: 再遷尚書，數納忠言，肅宗敬重之。
units.en: Promoted twice to director of the secretariat, he spoke plainly and often; Emperor Zhang held him in high regard.
units.literal: Twice transferred to Director of the Secretariat, he repeatedly submitted loyal words; Emperor Suzong respected him.

units.zh: 後以病乞骸骨，拜議郎，告歸，因稱病篤，帝賜以衣冠。
units.en: Later he asked to retire, was made gentleman consultant, went home pleading mortal illness, and received cap and gown from the throne.
units.literal: Later citing illness he begged for his bones, was appointed Gentleman Consultant, announced return home, thereupon claimed grave illness; the emperor bestowed on him cap and robes.

units.zh: 元和元年，詔告廬江太守、東平相曰：『議郎鄭均，束脩安貧，恭儉節整，前在機密，以病致仕，守善貞固，黃發不怠。
units.en: In Yuanhe 1 an edict told the governors of Lujiang and Dongping: 'Gentleman Consultant Zheng Jun lives frugally on a teacher's stipend, humble and orderly; he left confidential office for illness, keeps faith in old age, and never slackens.'
units.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe, an edict instructed the grand administrator of Lujiang and the minister of Dongping, saying, 'Gentleman Consultant Zheng Jun, with bundle of dried meat is content in poverty, respectful, frugal, restrained, and orderly; earlier in secretarial posts he retired on illness, guards goodness and is chaste and firm, yellow-haired without slackening.'

units.zh: 又前安邑令毛義，躬履遜讓，比征辭病，淳潔之風，東州稱仁。
units.en: Former magistrate Mao Yi of Anyi chose modest retirement over repeated calls—his purity is hailed as humanity in the eastern provinces.'
units.literal: Moreover, former chief of Anyi Mao Yi personally practiced yielding and modesty; whenever summoned he declined citing illness; the eastern provinces praise his pure and simple manner as benevolent.'

units.zh: 書不雲乎：「章厥有常，吉哉！」
units.en: The Documents put it this way: "When a ruler's rule holds steady, blessing follows!"
units.literal: Does not the Document say, "When good order has its constant rule, that is auspicious!"

units.zh: 其賜均、義谷各千斛，常以八月長吏存問，賜羊酒，顯茲異行。』
units.en: Grant each a thousand hu of grain; each eighth month let local officials call on them with sheep and wine to mark their rare virtue.'
units.literal: Let each be granted a thousand hu of grain; constantly in the eighth month let the senior clerk inquire after them and bestow sheep and wine, displaying these unusual conducts.'

units.zh: 明年，帝東巡過任城，乃幸均舍，敕賜尚書祿以終其身，故時人號為『白衣尚書』。
units.en: The next year, passing Rencheng on an eastern tour, the emperor called at Zheng Jun's home and granted him a director's salary for life—so men dubbed him the 'minister in plain clothes.'
units.literal: The next year, the emperor on eastern tour passed Rencheng, thereupon visited Jun's house, ordered bestowal of a Director of the Secretariat's salary for the rest of his life; therefore people of the time called him the "commoner Director of the Secretariat."

units.zh: 永元中，卒於家。
units.en: He died at home during the Yongyuan era.
units.literal: In the Yongyuan period, he died at home.

units.zh: 趙典字仲經，蜀郡成都人也。
units.en: Zhao Dian, styled Zhongjing, was from Chengdu in Shu commandery.
units.literal: Zhao Dian, courtesy name Zhongjing, was a man of Chengdu in Shujun commandery.

units.zh: 父戒，為太尉，桓帝立，以定策封廚亭侯。
units.en: His father Zhao Jie was grand commandant and, for fixing Emperor Huan's succession, was enfeoffed as marquis of Chuting.
units.literal: His father Jie was Grand Commandant; when Emperor Huan ascended, for planning the enthronement he was enfeoffed Marquis of Chuting.

units.zh: 典少篤行隱約，博學經書，弟子自遠方至。
units.en: Zhao Dian in youth was grave and retiring, wide-read in the classics, and drew students from afar.
