units.literal: Dian in youth was earnest in conduct, retiring and modest, broadly learned in the classics and scriptures, and disciples came from distant regions.

units.zh: 建和初，四府表薦，征拜議郎，侍講禁內，再遷為侍中。
units.en: Early in Jianhe the chief bureaus recommended him together; he became gentleman consultant, lectured inside the palace, and rose twice to palace attendant.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jianhe, the four offices jointly memorialized recommending him; he was summoned and appointed Gentleman Consultant, lectured within the forbidden precincts, and was twice transferred to Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 時，帝欲廣開鴻池，典諫曰：『鴻池泛溉，已且百頃，猶復增而深之，非所以崇唐、虞之約己，遵孝之愛人也。』
units.en: When the emperor planned to enlarge Hong Pool, Zhao Dian urged: 'It already floods nearly a hundred qing; to dig it wider and deeper is no way to honor the self-restraint of Yao and Shun or to show the humane care expected of a filial ruler.'
units.literal: At that time the emperor wished broadly to open Hong Pool; Dian remonstrated, saying, 'Hong Pool in flooding and irrigation is already nearly a hundred qing; again to increase and deepen it is not the means by which to honor Tang and Yu's restraint upon themselves or to practice filial piety's love for the people.'

units.zh: 帝納其言而止。
units.en: The emperor took his point and dropped the project.
units.literal: The emperor accepted his words and stopped.

units.zh: 父卒，襲封。
units.en: He succeeded to the title when his father died.
units.literal: When his father died, he inherited the fief.

units.zh: 出為弘農太守，轉右扶風。
units.en: He served as grand administrator of Hongnong, then as right administrator of Fufeng.
units.literal: He went out as grand administrator of Hongnong, then transferred to right Administrator of Fufeng.

units.zh: 公事去官，征拜城門校尉，轉將作大匠，遷少府，又轉大鴻臚。
units.en: He left office over an official matter, was recalled as colonel of the city gates, then court architect, privy treasurer, and finally grand herald.
units.literal: For public affairs he left office, was summoned and appointed Colonel of the City Gates, transferred to Court Architect, transferred to Privy Treasurer, again transferred to Grand Herald.

units.zh: 時，恩澤諸侯以無勞受封，群臣不悅而莫敢諫，典獨奏曰：『夫無功而賞，勞者不勸，上忝下辱，亂象幹度。
units.en: When court favorites won marquisates without service, the ministers fumed in silence; Zhao Dian alone wrote, 'Reward without work discourages the deserving, shames the throne, insults the people, and lets disorder mock Heaven's pattern.'
units.literal: At that time enfeoffed marquises of favor received fiefs without merit; the host of ministers was displeased yet none dared remonstrate; Dian alone submitted memorial, saying, 'When there is reward without merit, those who labor are not encouraged; above is shamed, below insulted, and disorderly signs interfere with the celestial norm.'

units.zh: 且高祖之誓，非功臣不封。
units.en: Moreover the founder swore that no man without merit should be enfeoffed.'
units.literal: Moreover Gaozu's oath was: unless a meritorious minister, do not enfeoff.'

units.zh: 宜一切削免爵士，以存舊典。』
units.en: Strip these sinecures away and restore the old standard.'
units.literal: It is fitting utterly to strip away titles and fiefs, in order to preserve the old norm.'

units.zh: 帝不從。
units.en: The emperor would not agree.
units.literal: The emperor did not follow.

units.zh: 頃之，轉太仆，遷太常。
units.en: Soon he moved to grand coachman, then grand master of ceremonies.
units.literal: Before long, he transferred to Grand Coachman, transferred to Grand Master of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 朝廷每有災異疑議，輒咨問之。
units.en: Whenever omens or disputed policy troubled the court, it turned to him for judgment.
units.literal: Whenever the court had prodigies or doubtful points for deliberation, it always consulted and asked him.

units.zh: 典據經正對，無所曲折。
units.en: Zhao Dian answered from the classics without trimming his words.
units.literal: Dian according to the classics answered straight, without twisting.

units.zh: 每得賞賜，輒分與諸生之貧者。
units.en: Every imperial gift he shared with his neediest pupils.
units.literal: Whenever he obtained rewards and gifts, he always divided them among the students who were poor.

units.zh: 後以諫爭違旨，免官就國。
units.en: He later lost office for opposing the throne too bluntly and retired to his fief.
units.literal: Later for remonstrating and disputing contrary to imperial intent, he was dismissed from office and went to his state.

units.zh: 會帝崩，時禁藩國諸侯不得奔吊，典慨然曰：『身從衣褐之中，致位上列。
units.en: When the emperor died, princes were barred from the capital for mourning; Zhao Dian declared, 'I rose from common cloth to the highest ranks.'
units.literal: When it happened that the emperor died, at that time it was forbidden for feudal princes of the kingdoms to hurry to mourning; Dian sighed with feeling, saying, 'My person from among coarse cloth has reached the upper ranks.'

units.zh: 且鳥烏反哺報德，況於士邪！』
units.en: Even crows feed their parents—should a scholar do less!'
units.literal: Moreover birds and crows in turning to feed repay virtue—how much more a gentleman!'

units.zh: 遂解印綬符策付縣，而馳到京師。
units.en: He handed his seal and credentials to the county magistrate and galloped to Luoyang.
units.literal: Thereupon he untied seal ribbons and tallies and handed them to the county, and galloped to the capital.

units.zh: 州郡及大鴻臚並執處其罪，而公卿百寮嘉典之義，表請以租自贖，詔書許之。
units.en: Province, commandery, and grand herald would have punished him, but the high ministers praised his devotion and memorialized to ransom his offense with grain, which the emperor allowed.
units.literal: Province, commandery, and Grand Herald together held him for his crime, but the dukes and ministers and hundred officials praised Dian's righteousness, memorialized asking to redeem with rent, and an edict permitted it.

units.zh: 再遷長樂少府、衛尉。
units.en: He was successively transferred to junior minister of Changle and commandant of the guards.
units.literal: Twice transferred to junior minister of Changle and Commandant of the Guards.

units.zh: 公卿復表典篤學博聞，宜備國師。
units.en: They again urged that Zhao Dian's learning fitted him to be tutor to the realm.
units.literal: The dukes and ministers again memorialized that Dian was earnest in learning and broadly heard, fitting to be prepared as state teacher.

units.zh: 會病卒，使者吊祠。
units.en: He died of illness first; the court sent envoys to his funeral.
units.literal: It happened that he died of illness; envoys attended mourning sacrifice.

units.zh: 竇太后復遣使兼贈印綬，謚曰獻侯。
units.en: Empress Dowager Dou sent envoys to confer his seals posthumously and named him Marquis Xian.
units.literal: Empress Dowager Dou again sent envoys concurrently to bestow seal ribbons, posthumous title Xian Marquis.

units.zh: 典兄子謙，謙弟溫，相繼為三公。
units.en: His nephews Zhao Qian and Zhao Wen each rose in turn to the three excellencies.
units.literal: Dian's elder brother's son Qian, Qian's younger brother Wen, in succession were the Three Dukes.

units.zh: 謙字產信，初平元年，代黃琬為太尉。
units.en: Zhao Qian, styled Chanxin, became grand commandant in Chuping 1, replacing Huang Wan.
units.literal: Qian, courtesy name Chanxin, in the first year of Chuping replaced Huang Wan as Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 獻帝遷都長安，以謙行車騎將軍，為前置。
units.en: When the capital moved to Chang'an, the emperor named Zhao Qian acting general of chariots and cavalry to lead the train.
units.literal: When Emperor Xian moved the capital to Chang'an, he made Qian act as general of chariots and cavalry and vanguard.

units.zh: 明年病罷。
units.en: Illness forced him out the following year.
units.literal: The next year he was dismissed for illness.

units.zh: 復為司隸校尉。
units.en: He was again appointed metropolitan commandant.
units.literal: Again he became Metropolitan Commandant.

units.zh: 車師王侍子為董卓所愛，數犯法，謙收殺之。
units.en: The Cheshi king's son, a hostage at court and Dong Zhuo's favorite, broke the law again and again until Zhao Qian seized him and put him to death.
units.literal: The hostage son of the king of Cheshi was favored by Dong Zhuo, repeatedly violated the law; Qian arrested and executed him.

units.zh: 卓大怒，殺都官從事，而素敬憚謙，故不加罪。
units.en: Dong Zhuo flew into a rage and executed Zhao Qian's retainer, yet he still respected Zhao Qian too much to touch him.
units.literal: Zhuo was greatly angry and killed the clerk for capital officials in his train, but had always revered and feared Qian, therefore did not add punishment to him.

units.zh: 轉為前將軍，遣擊白波賊，有功，封郫侯。
units.en: He was named former general, crushed the White Wave rebels, earned distinction, and was enfeoffed as marquis of Pi.
units.literal: He was transferred to be Former General, was sent to attack the White Wave bandits, had merit, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Pi.

units.zh: 李傕殺司徒王允，復代允為司徒。
units.en: When Li Jue murdered Minister Wang Yun, Zhao Qian stepped into Wang Yun's place as minister of education.
units.literal: Li Jue killed Minister of Education Wang Yun; Qian again replaced Yun as Minister of Education.

units.zh: 數月病免，拜尚書令。
units.en: A few months later illness forced him out; the court then named him director of the secretariat.
units.literal: Several months later he was dismissed for illness and appointed Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 是年卒，溢曰忠侯。
units.en: He died the same year and was given the posthumous title Marquis Zhong—'the Loyal.'
units.literal: That year he died; his posthumous title was Loyal Marquis.

units.zh: 溫字子柔，初為京兆丞，嘆曰：『大丈夫當雄飛，安能雌伏！』
units.en: Zhao Wen, styled Zirou, began as assistant governor of the capital region and swore, 'A true man should rise like a hawk, not hide like a mouse!'
units.literal: Wen, courtesy name Zirou, at first was assistant governor of the metropolitan region; he sighed, saying, 'A great man ought to soar like the male phoenix—how can he brood like the hen!'

units.zh: 遂棄官去。
units.en: He threw down his seal and walked away.
units.literal: Thereupon he abandoned office and departed.

units.zh: 遭歲大饑，散家糧以振窮餓，所活萬餘人。
units.en: When famine struck he opened his granaries to the starving and kept more than ten thousand souls alive.
units.literal: Encountering a year of great famine, he distributed the household's grain to relieve the starving and hungry; those he saved numbered more than ten thousand.

units.zh: 獻帝西遷都，為侍中，同輿輦至長安，封江南亭侯，代楊彪為司空，免，頃之，復為司徒，錄尚書事。
units.en: He rode west with Emperor Xian as palace attendant, won the title marquis of Jiangnan precinct, succeeded Yang Biao as minister of works, briefly lost the post, then returned as minister of education with authority over the secretariat.
units.literal: When Emperor Xian moved the capital west, he became Palace Attendant; together they rode the imperial carriage to Chang'an; he was enfeoffed Marquis of Jiangnan pavilion; he replaced Yang Biao as Minister of Works, was dismissed; before long again was Minister of Education, recording Director of Secretariat affairs.

units.zh: 時，李傕與郭汜相攻，傕遂虜掠禁省，動帝幸北塢，外內隔絕。
units.en: When Li Jue and Guo Si turned on each other, Li Jue sacked the palace, marched the emperor to the northern redoubt, and sealed the court off from the world.
units.literal: At that time Li Jue and Guo Si attacked each other; Jue thereupon plundered the forbidden precincts, moved the emperor to take refuge at the north stockade, and inside and outside were cut off.

units.zh: 傕素疑溫不與己同，乃內溫於塢中，又欲移乘輿於黃白城。
units.en: Li Jue had never trusted Zhao Wen; he locked him in the fortress and planned to drag the imperial train off to Huangbai.
units.literal: Jue had long suspected Wen did not share his aims; he thereupon shut Wen inside the stockade and again wished to move the imperial carriage to Huangbai City.

units.zh: 溫與傕書曰：『公前托為董公報仇，然實屠陷王城，殺戮大臣，天下不可家見而戶說也。
units.en: Zhao Wen wrote: 'You claimed to avenge Dong Zhuo, yet you gutted the capital and cut down the great ministers—no edict can whitewash that across every hearth.'
units.literal: Wen wrote to Jue, saying, 'Lord, you earlier claimed to avenge Lord Dong, yet in truth you butchered and trapped the royal capital and slaughtered great ministers—the realm cannot be shown house by house and explained door to door.'

units.zh: 今與郭汜爭睚眥之隙，以成千鈞之仇，人在塗炭，各不聊生。
units.en: Now you feud with Guo Si over a dirty look until the hatred weighs a thousand pounds, while the people burn in misery and barely survive.
units.literal: Now with Guo Si you contend over the grudge of a sidelong glance, thereby completing an enmity of a thousand jun; people are in mud and charcoal, each without means to live.

units.zh: 曾不改悟，遂成禍亂。
units.en: You refuse to repent, and chaos follows in your wake.
units.literal: You have not changed and awakened, and thereupon have become disaster and disorder.

units.zh: 朝廷仍下明詔，欲令和解。
units.en: The court has issued one clear order after another urging peace between you.
units.literal: The court repeatedly issued clear edicts, wishing to make you reconcile.

units.zh: 上命不行，威澤日損。
units.en: When imperial commands go unheeded, the throne's authority withers by the day.
units.literal: Superior commands are not carried out; might and grace are daily diminished.

units.zh: 而復欲移轉乘輿，更幸非所，此誠老夫所不達也。
units.en: Now you would haul the emperor off to yet another wrong refuge—an old minister like me cannot fathom such folly.
units.literal: Yet again you wish to move and turn the imperial carriage and again favor a place that is not right—this is truly what this old man cannot fathom.

units.zh: 於《易》，一為過，再為涉，三而弗改，滅其頂，兇。
units.en: The Book of Changes warns: one slip is error, a second time you ford deep water, a third without reform brings ruin on your own head.
units.literal: In the Changes, once is fault, twice is fording, thrice without change—'destroy his crown,' inauspicious.

units.zh: 不如早共和解，引軍還屯，上安萬乘，下全人民，豈不幸甚。』
units.en: Better make peace now, pull your troops back to camp, secure the sovereign above and spare the people below—nothing could bring greater good fortune."
units.literal: It would be better early together to reconcile, to draw the army back and encamp, above to pacify the ten thousand chariots, below to preserve the people—how could that not be greatly fortunate."

units.zh: 傕大怒，欲遣人殺溫。
units.en: Li Jue raged and ordered Zhao Wen killed.
units.literal: Jue was greatly angry and wished to send men to kill Wen.

units.zh: 李傕從弟應，溫故掾也，諫之數日，乃獲免。
units.en: Li Ying, Li Jue's cousin and once Zhao Wen's clerk, argued for days until Li Jue relented.
units.literal: Li Jue's cousin Ying, Wen's former clerk, remonstrated for several days, and then he obtained exemption.

units.zh: 溫從車駕都許。
units.en: Zhao Wen followed the court when it settled at Xu.
units.literal: Wen followed the imperial carriage to the capital at Xu.

units.zh: 建安十三年，以辟司空曹操子丕為掾，操怒，奏溫辟臣子弟，選舉不實，免官。
units.en: In Jian'an 13 he recruited Cao Pi as a clerk in the ministry of works; Cao Cao, furious, impeached him for nepotism in appointments and stripped him of office.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jianan, for having summoned Minister of Works Cao Cao's son Pi as clerk, Cao was angry and memorialized that Wen in summoning sons of ministers had selection and promotion untrue to fact, and he was dismissed from office.

units.zh: 是歲卒，年七十二。
units.en: He died the same year at seventy-two.
units.literal: That year he died, aged seventy-two.

units.zh: 贊曰：宣、鄭、二王，奉身清方。
units.en: Summing up: Xuan Bing, Zheng Jun, and the two Wangs kept their lives as straight as a line.
units.literal: The encomium says: Xuan, Zheng, and the two Wangs held their persons pure and upright.

units.zh: 杜林據古，張湛矜莊。
units.en: Du Lin stood on the old texts; Zhang Zhan wore dignity like armor.
units.literal: Du Lin relied on antiquity; Zhang Zhan was stern and dignified.

units.zh: 典以義黜，宮由德揚。
units.en: Zhao Dian fell for speaking truth; Cheng Gong rose on quiet merit.
units.literal: Dian by righteousness was demoted; Gong by virtue was raised.

units.zh: 大儀鵠發，見表憲王。
units.en: Wu Dayi spread his wings like a swan and became the mirror held up to Prince Xian of Dongping.
units.literal: Dayi took flight like a swan, and was seen as a model for the Prince of Dongping.

units.zh: 少卿誌仕，終乘高箱。
units.en: Guo Shaoqing vowed his way to rank and at last rode the tall chariot he had promised himself.
units.literal: Shaoqing set his will on office, and in the end rode the high carriage.

units.zh: 鄭興、賈逵，以附同稱顯；
units.en: Zheng Xing and Jia Kui climbed to prominence by swimming with the tide;
units.literal: Zheng Xing and Jia Kui, by going along with the trend, won renown;

units.zh: 史臣曰：昔鄧禹基於文學，杜預出自儒雅，卒致軍功，名著前代。
units.en: The historian writes: Deng Yu began in the classics and Du Yu in pure scholarship, yet both won fame in war and live in the histories of old.
units.literal: The historian says: In old times Deng Yu rose from literary study and Du Yu came out of refined Confucian learning, yet in the end they achieved military merit and their fame stands in former ages.

units.zh: 沛相陈珪举孝廉，太尉黄琬辟，皆不就。
units.en: Pei chancellor Chen Gui nominated him filial and incorrupt; Minister Huang Wan called him to office—he declined both.
units.literal: The chancellor of Pei, Chen Gui, recommended him as Filial and Incorrupt; Minister of Works Huang Wan summoned him; in neither case did he go.

units.zh: 後太守鮑昱請獲，既至門，令主簿就迎，主簿但使騎吏迎之，獲聞之，即去。
units.en: Governor Bao Yu later invited him in, yet at the door the chief clerk sent only outriders instead of greeting him in person; Gao Huo turned on his heel.
units.literal: Later, when Governor Bao Yu invited Huo, and Huo had reached the gate, Yu ordered his chief clerk to go welcome him in person, but the chief clerk merely sent mounted clerks to receive him; when Huo heard of it, he departed at once.

units.zh: 昱自往問何以致雨，獲曰：「急罷三部督郵，明府當自北出，到三十里亭，雨可致也。」
units.en: Bao Yu rode out to ask the rite for rain. Gao Huo said, 'Dismiss your three touring supervisors at once, then ride north yourself to the thirty-li post station—that will draw the storm.'
units.literal: Yu himself went to ask by what means rain could be brought; Huo said, 'Hurry to dismiss the three circuit supervising clerks; my enlightened lord should himself ride north to the post station at thirty li, and rain can be brought.'

units.zh: 昱從之，果得大雨。
units.en: Bao Yu obeyed, and the heavens opened.
units.literal: Yu followed him, and indeed obtained great rain.

units.zh: 昱遣追請獲，獲顧曰：「府君但為主簿所欺，不足與談。」
units.en: Bao Yu sent runners to fetch him back; Gao Huo called over his shoulder, 'Your honor is hoodwinked by a clerk—not worth my time.'
units.literal: Yu sent men in pursuit to invite Huo again; Huo looked back and said, 'The lord of the house is merely deceived by his chief clerk—not worth talking with.'

units.zh: 每行縣，輒軾其閭。
units.en: Whenever Bao Yu inspected the counties he lifted the carriage bar in salute as he passed Gao Huo's lane.
units.literal: Whenever he toured the counties, he always touched the crossbar of his carriage in respect at Huo's lane.

units.zh: 茂陵杜鄴與欽同姓字，俱以材能稱京師，故衣冠謂欽為「盲杜子夏」以相別。
units.en: Another Du Ye of Maoling shared his surname and courtesy name; both were known in Chang'an for their gifts, so the gentry dubbed our man "the blind Du Zixia" to tell the two apart.
units.literal: Maoling Du Ye with Qin had the same surname and courtesy, both by talent and ability were praised in the capital; therefore caps and robes called Qin "Blind Du Zixia" to distinguish.

units.zh: 欽惡以疾見詆，乃為小冠，高廣財二寸，由是京師更謂欽為「小冠杜子夏」，而鄴為「大冠杜子夏」云。
units.en: Qin resented the nickname, so he took to wearing a tiny cap barely two inches high and wide; thereafter Chang'an called him "Little-Cap Du Zixia" and the other "Big-Cap Du Zixia."
units.literal: Qin hated being seen slandered by illness, and therefore made a small cap, high and wide only two cun; from this the capital further called Qin "Small-cap Du Zixia," while Ye was "Large-cap Du Zixia," it is said.

units.zh: 臣朔年二十二，長九尺三寸，目若懸珠，齒若編貝，勇若孟賁，捷若慶忌，廉若鮑叔，信若尾生。
units.en: I am twenty-two, stand nine feet three inches, my eyes shine like pearls and my teeth line up like shells; in courage I match Meng Ben, in agility Qingji, in integrity Bao Shu, in good faith Weisheng.
units.literal: Your servant Shuo is twenty-two years old, nine feet three inches tall, with eyes like suspended pearls and teeth like strung shells, brave as Meng Ben, swift as Qingji, incorrupt as Bao Shu, trustworthy as Weisheng.

units.zh: 北海周澤、瑯邪承宮並海內大儒，鯈皆以為師友而致之於朝。
units.en: Zhou Ze of Beihai and Cheng Gong of Langya were both leading scholars of the realm; Fan Tiao took both as teacher-friends and brought them to court.
units.literal: Zhou Ze of Beihai and Cheng Gong of Langya were both great Confucian scholars within the realm; Tiao took both as teacher-friends and brought them to court.

units.zh: 又多徵名儒，以充禮官，如沛國趙孝、瑯邪承宮等，或安車結駟，告歸鄉里；
units.en: Famous scholars such as Zhao Xiao of Pei and Cheng Gong of Langye filled ritual posts—some rode home in honor carriages;
units.literal: Moreover many were summoned, famous scholars, to fill ritual offices, such as Zhao Xiao of Pei state, Cheng Gong of Langye, and others—some with secure carriages and four-horse teams, announcing return to village lanes;

units.zh: 臣愚以為宜下明詔，博求幽隱，發揚巖穴，寵進儒雅，有如孝、宮者，徵詣公車，以侯聖上講習之期。
units.en: Issue an edict summoning hidden scholars and men of learning like Zhao Xiao and Cheng Gong to the capital to await your lectures.
units.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks it fitting to issue a clear edict, broadly seek the hidden and concealed, raise up cliff and cave, favor and advance Confucian elegance—such as Xiao and Gong—summon them to the public carriage, to await the sage superior's period of lecturing and practice.

units.zh: 稚季者大俠，與衛尉淳于長、大鴻臚蕭育等皆厚善。
units.en: Du Zhiji was tied to Chunyu Zhang and Xiao Yu.
units.literal: Zhiji was a great bravo, thick with Commandant of the Guards Chunyu Zhang and grand herald Xiao Yu.

units.zh: 會淳于長敗，寶與蕭育等皆坐免官。
units.en: Chunyu Zhang's fall swept Sun Bao and Xiao Yu out with him.
units.literal: When Chunyu Zhang fell, Bao and Xiao Yu and others were all dismissed for implication.

units.zh: 詔曰：「豫寧縣開國伯、新除散騎常侍、領左軍將軍馮道根，奉上能忠，有功不伐，撫人留愛，守邊難犯，祭遵、馮異、郭伋、李牧，不能過也。
units.en: The edict said, "Feng Daogen, founding Count of Yuning county, newly appointed Regular Attendant and acting Left Army General, served his sovereign with loyalty, had merit without boasting, governed the people and left affection behind, and defended the frontier so that it was hard to violate; Ji Zun, Feng Yi, Guo Ji, and Li Mu could not surpass him.
units.literal: The edict said, "Feng Daogen, founding Count of Yuning county, newly appointed Regular Attendant and acting Left Army General, served his sovereign with loyalty, had merit without boasting, governed the people and left affection behind, and defended the frontier so that it was hard to violate; Ji Zun, Feng Yi, Guo Ji, and Li Mu could not surpass him.
